**LIBRARY v1** (`library/`, Library / Βιβλιοθήκη, 1.08.00)
- `library`: Library / Βιβλιοθήκη, category **Personal**, right after Media Shelf (Chris 2026-10-12 11:38 "Ναι σε όλα"). EPUB and PDF reader for books on the orOS disk. Universal search provider `library/search.js` (books, highlights and noted bookmarks; target `{ book, loc? }`).
- Slice `library` (`oros-library-data`): `{ ver:1, books:[], pos:{}, marks:[], tombs:{} }`. Books, positions and marks are LWW by `m` (tie: larger canonical JSON), tombstones keep the max and hide records with `m <= tomb`. Merge symmetric, associative, idempotent, output canonical (tests/library.test.js).
- Device-local: `oros-library-prefs` (reading settings, view, sort, filter, side panel), `oros-library-paths` (path → size, mtime, book id; avoids re-hashing), IndexedDB `oros-library-cache` (cover thumbnails).
- File handler: `.epub` and `.pdf` open in Library ("Open with"; PDF was not taken by any app before).
- Book id = "b" + first 16 hex of the file's SHA-256: the same file on two devices is the same book, wherever it sits. `path` is a synced hint only; each device maps ids to its own paths.
- Locations: EPUB `e:<spine>:<offset in the chapter's text-node string>`; PDF `p:<page>:<offset in the page text>` (items + "\n" at EOL, same as the text layer DOM) or `p:<page>:y<per-mille>` for a place on the page. Highlights keep quote + 32-char context and re-anchor by quote when the offset no longer matches.
- Books the disk scan finds by itself get `m = 1`, so a record from another device (edits, finished date) always wins; a new device scanning before its first pull never overwrites them. The saved place is not rewritten while it is still on screen (other screen sizes start pages elsewhere).
- **Phase 2–3 (1.20.00):** read aloud (`library/speak.js`, `speechSynthesis` one sentence at a time, `core.speechParts`; pause = cancel keeping the sentence; key S); reading stats (`library/stats.js`) in the synced slice as `stats: { d: {day: {device: secs}}, b: {book: {device: secs}} }`, each device only adds to its own counter, merge = max per counter, 400 days kept, device id `oros-library-dev` device-local; Send to Notes (`__orosOpenAt("notes", { add })`, ≤ 20,000 chars); Today provider `library/today.js` (apps.json `"today": ["core.js", "today.js"]`, read-only, one line: current book, progress, today's time, streak).
- FB2 (incl. `.fb2.zip`, any declared encoding) and CBZ (≤ 200 MB, ComicInfo.xml) become a small in-memory EPUB (`core` §12, `store.memZip`, `fb2Zip`, `cbzZip`) through the same sanitizer; records keep `fmt: "epub"` + `kind: "fb2" | "cbz"`. `.fb2` / `.cbz` added to BR-FILE-OPEN (TWA / MSIX packages need regenerating).
- Look-up (`library/lookup.js`, `core` §13): Wiktionary REST definitions, text only, after a one-time opt-in per device, only the word is sent. Ask the Assistant (word in its sentence via engine hook `sentenceAt`, a passage, or the whole book without spoilers) through `__orosOpenAt("assistant", { ask })` ≤ 2000 chars; nothing is sent until the user sends it.
- **Wave 33 — online catalogues, CBR, Markdown export:**
  - Slice gains `cats:[{id "c"+[0-9a-z]{6,24}, m, url (http/https, ≤ 500; the add form also refuses user:password@), name ≤ 80}]` (the user's own OPDS catalogues, ≤ 50, LWW by m, removal = tombstone under the same `tombs`; the key is left out while empty, so older devices' bytes are unchanged; an older device drops `cats` in its own copy and the union restores it on the next merge). Built-ins are code, never stored: Project Gutenberg (`https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks.opds/`, search `ebooks/search.opds/?query={searchTerms}`) and Standard Ebooks' free new-releases Atom feed (`https://standardebooks.org/feeds/atom/new-releases`, EPUB `rel="enclosure"` links); SE's full OPDS feed needs a Patrons Circle login, so it is not used. Device-local `oros-library-prefs`.opds = true after the one-time note.
  - `library/opds.js` (`window.LibOpds`, pure, Node-testable: `parseFeed` Atom OPDS 1.x + OPDS 2 JSON incl. groups, acquisition / enclosure / thumbnail links, OpenSearch `parseOsd`, `searchUrl` for `{searchTerms}` and `{?query}` templates, `sniffOk` by magic bytes, `absUrl` http(s) only — images https only, `fileName`). All feed text is plain text (inline tags stripped, then `textContent`); no markup or script from a feed reaches the DOM. `library/catalog.js` is the UI (`LIB.catalog.open`), loading `../feeds/core.js` + `../feeds/fetch.js` lazily: direct GET first, then the Mail relay's `web` op (≤ 5 MB a response) when CORS blocks; without a relay → "norelay" message. Downloads are checked (size, magic bytes) and go through `LIB.store.addFile` like a local import (to `/internal/Books`).
  - CBR (RAR comics): `kind: "cbr"` (fmt stays "epub"; a record with no `kind` but a `.cbr` path is read as cbr). `store.cbrZip` lazy-imports the vendored libarchive.js 2.0.2 (`vendor/libarchive/`: `libarchive.js` ES module, `worker-bundle.js` module worker, `libarchive.wasm`; loaded only when a .cbr is opened), refuses encrypted archives ("drm"), reads a ZIP-in-disguise as CBZ, then the CBZ path (`C.cbzBook` → `packBook` → `memZip`). ≤ 200 MB like CBZ. `.cbr` is not yet in BR-FILE-OPEN (shell-owned).
  - Markdown export: `core.exportMarkdown(book, marks, lang, labels, opts)` — with `opts.date` a Readwise / Obsidian-style header (`- Author:`, `- Highlights: N · Notes: M`, `- Exported: <date> from orOS Library`), chapter `##` sections, `>` quotes, colour · place %, note below; without `opts` the old output is unchanged. `core.notesMarkdown(book, marks, lang, {max, date, labels})` → `{text, left}` is what Send to Notes now sends (Markdown, ≤ 20,000 chars, "… and N more"). No change in Notes (`__orosOpenAt("notes", { add })` already existed).
  - Tests: `tests/library-opds.test.js` (OPDS 1/2 parsing, OpenSearch, URL safety, sniffing, cats merge/tombs, Markdown export).

**MONTAGE v1** (`montage/core.js`, slice `montage`, key `oros-montage`; video editor, plan `/mnt/project-files/video-editor/video-editor-plan.md`, Chris 2026-10-12 "Ναι σε όλα"; registered at 1.10.00):

```
oros-montage = { ver:1, projects{ <pid>: project }, tombs{ <pid>: ms } }
project = { id, name, ar: "16:9"|"9:16"|"1:1"|"4:5", fps: 30|60, bg:"#rrggbb", vs: bool, dk?: 1-90, m, items{ <iid>: item }, tombs{ <iid>: ms } }
item    = { id, k: video|image|audio|title, tr: main|ov|tt|a1|a2, m, … }
```

- Tracks: `main` is magnetic (order key `o`, clips follow each other, a transition `tx{k: fade|black|slide|wipe|push|zoom|circle, d}` overlaps the clip before, at most half of either clip); `ov` (picture in picture), `tt` (titles), `a1`/`a2` (sound) use a start `at`. Which kinds go on which track: `TRACK_KINDS`.
- video/audio: `src`, `len` (file length), `in`/`out` (seconds in the file), `sp` 0.25-4, `vol` 0-200, `mu`; image: `src`, `d`; title: `d`, `text{t,f,sz,col,ol,bx,al,an}` (+ `bg` on main = a title card). Pictures also `op`, `fit` fit|fill, `rot`, `fl`, `lk{b,c,s,t}`, `flt`; off-main pictures `box{x,y,w,h}`; all `fi`/`fo` fades.
- Media are never in the slice: `src` is an orOS disk id `/internal/Assets/<sha256>.<ext>` in the forms Atelier's `clips.js` and `designkit/assets.js` use (jpg|png, webm|mp4, mp3|m4a|ogg|wav|weba), so Atelier's "unused files" check sees them as in use. `vs` = this project's media travel through Vault Drive (off by default: device only).
- **Merge:** projects and items are separate entities, LWW by their own `m` (tie → greater canonical JSON); tombstones max-union, per project and per item; a project survives its tombstone when any edit in it is newer (R17). Strict normalizer drops invalid rows; output canonical (keys sorted). Edits stamp `m` at the mutation site, always forward (R27). Tests: `tests/montage.test.js`.
- Rendering: `framePlan(project, t)` (layers on screen) and `soundPlan(project)` (sound segments) are the single source for preview and export; `montage/gl.js` draws a plan (WebGL2), `montage/export.js` encodes frame by frame with WebCodecs via `vendor/mediabunny.min.js`.
- Phase 2 wave 1 (no new item fields): `dk` = ducking, % the Music row (`a1`) drops while anything sounds on Voice (`a2`), 0.25 s ramps, applied in `gainAt` so preview and export match. It is written only when on (absent = off), so a project without ducking is byte-identical on copies that predate it. Subtitles are ordinary `tt` titles (`SUB_BOX` style); `parseSrt`/`toSrt` read SRT and WebVTT (markup dropped, at most 1500 cues) and write SRT. Freeze frame = the video splits at the playhead and a full-size PNG of that frame (`MontageMedia.frameAt`, imported like any picture) goes between as a 2 s image (`freezeAt`). Filters added: vintage, chrome, dusk, golden. Sound-only export: M4A (AAC), else Ogg (Opus), else WAV; "keep a copy" goes to `/internal/Music/`.
- Phase 2 wave 2, keyframes: optional item field `kf = [{ t, x, y, s, o, v }]` (t seconds into the clip, sorted, one key per t, at most 60; pictures and titles take x/y −2..2 (fraction of the frame), s 0.1–5, o 0–100; video and sound take v 0–200; values r3). Written only when the clip has keys. Linear between keys (so a split at any time keeps the motion exactly; `split` adds a key at the cut on both halves), held before the first and after the last. `framePlan` turns them into the layer box (main clips get a box around the full frame) and alpha; `soundPlan` passes volume keys as `kv` to `gainAt`. Keys are relative to the clip start, so trimming the start shifts them.
- Phase 2 wave 3A: `rv: true` (video only) plays a clip backwards from its out point, silent (left out of `soundPlan`); `split` cuts a reversed clip from the out side. Export decodes reversed clips in forward runs of 15 frames handed out backwards (decoders only run forwards). `lut` (picture id) = a colour look from a `.cube` 3D LUT (2-64 points a side, DOMAIN_MIN/MAX honoured), stored as an n²×n PNG (blue slices side by side, red along x, green down y) through the normal picture import, so it lives on the device or syncs with the project's media like any picture; `mediaOf` and relink include it; MontageGL samples it on texture unit 1 after the filter. GIF export: 12 fps, long side 320 or 480 px, at most 30 s, silent, one popularity palette (5 bits a channel) per frame, LZW in `export.js` (`GifWriter`, no library); kept copies go to `/internal/Pictures/`.
- Phase 2 wave 3B: kind `shape` (Overlay row only) with `sh` {k, col, ol, ow} written only for shapes; `k` one of rect, round, ellipse, triangle, star, heart, arrow, bubble; `col` "" = no fill, `ow` 0-20, and normalize forces an outline when there is no fill and no outline width, so a shape is never invisible. Fit, rotate, flip, look, filter and LUT stay video/picture only. MontageGL draws shapes on a 2D canvas through the titles cache, so they take box, opacity, keyframes and transitions like any layer. Stickers are plain titles (emoji, size 18, `pop` entrance) on the Text row, no new field. Light copies (proxies): `Make light copies` in Project settings converts videos whose short side is over 540 px to 540 px copies (`proxy-<id>.webm|mp4`, Mediabunny `Conversion`, no sound) in the device media store; device-only, never synced, never in `mediaOf`; the player prefers them, export and `Grab frame` (now `MontageExport.still`, rendered from the originals at the project size) never use them; `Free space` keeps a proxy only while its original is still used.
- Wave 41 (parity with CapCut / Clipchamp / Shotcut). Five optional item fields, each written only when in use, so older projects stay byte-identical; invalid values are dropped or clamped by the normalizer; merge is unchanged (LWW per item, so a field travels with its item's `m`):
  - `sr` (video/audio) = speed curve `[{s, v}]`: `s` seconds in the file (sorted, inside `in..out`), `v` 0.1-10; 2-20 keys; linear in file time between keys, held outside. While `sr` exists `sp` is ignored. Clip time is ∫ds/v (per piece `L·ln(v1/v0)/(v1−v0)`), inverted in closed form (`fwdPos`/`fwdLocal`), cached per item (WeakMap). Keys live in file time, so `split` (cut at `fwdPos`) and trims never move them; reverse reads `fwdPos(dur − t)`. Presets (`RAMPS`: hero, bullet, montage, jump, flashin, flashout) are shapes scaled onto `in..out`. Preview: media element `playbackRate = rateAt(t)`, updated as it changes. Export sound: `srcPieces` cuts each window into 50 ms pieces of one rate each, every piece an `AudioBufferSourceNode` at that `playbackRate` (pitch follows speed, as with `sp`).
  - `ck` (video/image) = chroma key `{col, tol 0-100, soft 0-100, sp 0-100}`: distance in the CbCr plane (OBS-style), similarity `tol/100·0.3`, smoothness `soft/100·0.2`, spill `sp/100·0.3` (desaturates towards the key); in the MontageGL shader right after the texture fetch, so preview and export match. `Pick from the picture` averages 5×5 pixels of the stage canvas.
  - `bd` (video/image) = picture-in-picture frame `{w 0-10 (% of the frame's short side), col, r 0-50 (% of the box's short side)}`: rounded corners and border drawn by an SDF in the shader (`borderPx`), inside the box.
  - `fc` (video/image) = reframe focus keys `[{t, x, y}]` (≤ 60): `t` file seconds for video (clip seconds for pictures), `x`/`y` 0-1 in source coordinates before rotate/mirror (`shownPoint`/`uvOf` map them); used only when `fit` = fill (`placeIn` clamps the focus so the picture still covers the box). Auto reframe (`montage/reframe.js`): Mediabunny CanvasSink at 480 px, 3 samples/s (≤ 180); `FaceDetector` where the browser has it, else a centre-weighted motion centroid (frame difference) with a detail fallback; then smoothing and Ramer-Douglas-Peucker down to few keys. `Reframe all clips` (Project settings) = one undo step.
  - `na` (video/audio) = id of a cleaned sound file (noise removed), a normal sound media id: `soundPlan` plays it instead of `src` (same timing), `mediaOf`/relink/`replaceSrc` include it, relinking `src` to a different file drops it, `detachSound` carries `sr` and `na`. Clips of the same `src` reuse one `na`. Made by `montage/denoise.js`: RNNoise v0.1.1 (BSD-3, Xiph.Org / Mozilla / Amazon, original model) compiled to `vendor/rnnoise/rnnoise.wasm` (118 KB) with clang + wasm-ld and a tiny own libc shim (no Emscripten, no imports; build script and shim in `vendor/rnnoise/build/`), fetched on first use, not precached. Mediabunny `Conversion` with `audio.process` at 48 kHz, ≤ 2 channels, 480-sample frames, int16 scale, the 480-sample delay compensated → M4A (AAC), else Ogg (Opus), else WAV, imported like any sound.
  - Automatic subtitles (`montage/asr.js`, no new field: the result is ordinary `tt` subtitle titles via `addSubtitles`): OpenAI Whisper tiny (MIT; ONNX q8 export by Xenova, Apache-2.0) on the vendored ONNX Runtime Web (`vendor/ort/`, one thread), the same way Atelier runs u2netp, with no library around it: log-mel (Slaney mel table, checked against Whisper's `mel_filters.npz`), greedy decoding with Whisper's timestamp rules and KV cache (merged decoder), byte-level BPE text. Nothing is fetched until the user presses `Make subtitles` under a size notice; then the runtime (≈ 11 MB, same origin) and the model (≈ 42 MB: encoder, merged decoder, vocab.json, generation_config.json from `huggingface.co/Xenova/whisper-tiny`, the only third-party host) go into IndexedDB `oros-montage-ai` (version `ort1.22.0-whisper-tiny-q8`); `Remove the speech model` clears it. Input = the export sound mix (`MontageExport.speech16k`: mono, decimated 48 → 16 kHz per 10 s window), at most the first 30 minutes; 30 s windows, silent windows skipped, language `auto`/`en`/`el` (device-local pref `asr`), lines over 84 characters split by words. Sound never leaves the device.
  - Tests: `tests/montage-effects.test.js` (time remapping, keys, crop maths, chroma, border, subject finder, RNNoise stream with the real wasm, Whisper's pure steps and decoding loop with a scripted model).

## Part V — Sync + data-safety essentials

### Security model (absolute)

- Zero tracking. Zero-knowledge passphrase (AES-GCM + PBKDF2, client-side): 600,000 rounds for new writes since A70 (2026-10-07), 100,000 for blobs without `iter`. A passphrase being SET (empty cloud, change) needs at least 10 characters.
- Dropbox tokens are used only for file I/O (PKCE). Vault: sealed passphrase + IndexedDB NON-EXTRACTABLE key, opt-in per device.
- All third-party-cloud data MUST be E2EE, for any future provider too.
- **One cloud owner (R34):** `sync.js` holds the only OAuth handler and the only token state. Slice data and Vault Drive are separate channels in the same app folder (Part II).
- App frames are same-origin with the shell. **XSS in any app = full access to tokens and data.** Treat every import as hostile:
  - Sanitize in an INERT document (`document.implementation.createHTMLDocument`). `innerHTML` on a live-document element fires `<img onerror>` even when detached.
  - `esc()` does not escape quotes; use `escAttr()` in attributes and quote-escape URL captures.

### Data-safety supremacy (zero-loss guarantee)

- **Sync:** bidirectional push-pull, deterministic merges.
- **Automatic backup = folder backup [log, v0.38.25–26]:**
  - The localStorage auto-snapshot subsystem is RETIRED (it filled the shared quota, R30). The line that stood here ("rolling 5 full-DB auto-snapshots, oros-auto-snapshots, Restore picker") described it.
  - What remains: export to a user-chosen folder through the File System Access API. **Chromium desktop only**, progressive enhancement.
  - `maybeAutoExport`: daily / weekly / monthly, checked at boot and on tab-visible, no timers. The body is captured live by `exportBodyNow()` (inside try/catch).
  - Files `orOS-backup-YYYY-MM-DD.json` (`writeBackupFile`). `wipeFolderMirror` also cleans legacy `orOS-snapshot-*.json`.
  - Permission-lapse detection with one-click Reconnect. `state.autoexport` travels in the shell slice.
  - Firefox and mobile have no automatic local export (no File System Access API). Accepted (decision 2026-10-05): there the safety net is Dropbox sync + manual export.
- **Manual export:** full DB, every parameter; import restores zero-loss (through `applyPayload`, merge-aware). **[log]** The shell buttons and Ctrl+Alt+Shift+X go through `shellSaveJson` / `shellPickJson` (R33).
- **Close safety net:** on-close sync + `beforeunload` warning when dirty and online.
- **Factory reset:** double confirm → cloud → folder → localStorage prefix sweep → OrosFS wipe → **[log]** Cache Storage `oros-map-tiles` → reload. Everything is tombstoned and seeds are reborn.
- **Corruption:** rescue backup before any reseed. **Compatibility:** additive migrations; unknown fields carried forward.
- **Quota (R30):** one shared ~5 MB `localStorage`. A failed `setItem` means edits will not survive a reload, so warn the user.
- **No re-upload of what the cloud holds (SY-L1, 0.48.02):** after a pull applies a slice, the engine compares what the slice STORES (`get()` after `set()`) with the cloud copy, not the merge output. An app whose store normalizes the merge result differently no longer re-uploads at every reconcile. Apps should still keep `merge(x, null)` idempotent (store == merge output).
- **Visible failure reason (SY-L2, 0.48.02):** a failed background sync logs `orOS sync: auto sync (<reason>) failed:` in the console and shows the reason in the sync dot tooltip and the menu's sync section (generic errors carry the technical text, e.g. `upload failed: 429`) until the next successful sync. No toast, no inbox entry (A72 still open).

### Files-disk glue (`shell.js` §9f)

- `files.js` mutates → `__orosFilesDiskTouched()` (engine dirty + 1s-debounced cache refresh).
- Remote data while the app is closed sets a pending flag, consumed at the next open.
- `fdSliceGet` is PURE. `fdRefreshForExport()` guarantees a live snapshot before manual exports.

## Part VI — Canonical patterns (verbatim contracts)

Status per pattern: **[re-verified 2026-10-01]**, **[carried]** (from earlier revisions) or **[log]** (from session notes after 2026-10-01). Check the last two against the file before relying on them.

### Boot sequence [carried]

`load()` → `applyI18n()` → paint static aria/icons → `wire()` → `registerSync()` → `inheritPalette()` → `watchPalette()` → reset view state → first render (single pass) → consume staged deep link AFTER first paint.

**Invoke `boot()` at the END of the IIFE** (after every `let`/`const`): a boot triggered early hits TDZ errors on later declarations.

### Three things every sync slice must get right (2026-10-06)

1. The merge function is the FIFTH ARGUMENT of `registerSlice`. A union written inside the setter never runs: for a slice without `mergeFn` the engine decides "local or remote" by itself and may never call the setter.
2. The getter returns a canonical COPY of the data that travels, and nothing else: no device-local or volatile fields (sweep stamps, caches, timers). One field that moves by itself makes the slice "always changed" and every sync cycle uploads.
3. Whatever prunes locally by the clock must also prune inside the merge with the same rule, or the pruned entry returns with every pull.

### Boot marker [re-verified in Writer]

```js
var SCRIPT_V = "";
(function () {
  var m = (document.currentScript && document.currentScript.src || "").match(/[?&]v=([^&#]+)/);
  SCRIPT_V = m ? m[1] : "";
  console.log("<app>.js v" + (SCRIPT_V || "?") + " boot");
})();
```

### Shell API + language resolution in an app frame (R8) [re-verified]

```js
function syncApi() {
  try { return (window.parent && window.parent.orosSync) || window.orosSync || null; }
  catch (e) { return window.orosSync || null; }
}
// Language: shell writes localStorage "oros-lang" and reopens apps on toggle.
function appLang() {
  try {
    var l = localStorage.getItem("oros-lang") ||
            (window.parent && window.parent.orosLang) || "en";
    return l === "el" ? "el" : "en";
  } catch (e) { return "en"; }
}
```

### Sync registration + dirty funnel [carried; canonical rule re-verified]

```js
function registerSync() {
  // LOCAL FIRST: load() MUST have run before this (boot order). Live
  // registration does NOT hydrate the app — registering an empty state
  // lets the first get()/save() persist and push an empty slice.
  var api = syncApi();
  window.__orosSyncApi = { _suppress:false, dirty:function(){
    if (this._suppress) return;
    if (api && typeof api.markDirty === "function") api.markDirty(); } };
  if (!api || typeof api.registerSlice !== "function") return;
  api.registerSlice("<id>", sliceGet, sliceSet, STORAGE_KEY, mergeFn);   // 5 args, always
}
```

- `save()`: `localStorage.setItem` + `__orosSyncApi.dirty()`.
- `sliceSet(data, info)`:
  - if the user has pending edits, fold them in first (`mergeFn(serialize(), data)`);
  - write + persist the storage key, with NO `markDirty` (R6);
  - normalize, sanitize view state, re-render (keep the caret when the content is unchanged);
  - no toast (sync feedback is the taskbar dot).
- `serialize()` must be canonical (R26): arrays sorted by id, tombstones canonical, no device-local fields.

### Notification trigger [re-verified against notifications.js 0.38.12]

```js
function notifyDue(key, title, body, deepLink) {
  var n = null;
  try { n = window.parent && window.parent.orosNotifs; } catch (e) {}
  if (n && typeof n.emit === "function") {
    return n.emit({ ns: "<appid>", key: key, title: title, body: body,
                    deepLink: deepLink /* "<appid>:<payload>" */ }) !== null;
  }
  return false;   // caller falls back to its legacy local alert
}
```

### Transient note / toasts [re-verified]

```js
function showToast(msg) {            // informational → shell transient
  try {
    var n = (window.parent && window.parent.orosNotifs) || window.orosNotifs;
    if (n && typeof n.transient === "function" &&
        n.transient({ ns: "<appid>", title: String(msg) })) return;
  } catch (e) {}
  localToast(msg);                   // stale bundle / standalone fallback
}
```

- **Undo-bearing toasts stay LOCAL** (closure never leaves the frame), 8s.
- **A modal `<dialog>` makes the rest of the page inert:** host the local toast inside the top-most `dialog[open]`, and move it back to `<body>` when that dialog closes.
- **[log]** `transient` bypasses app toggles, accepts any `ns`, and returns the item id, or `null` when not ready. An app that only uses transient toasts does not need a `KNOWN_APPS` entry (Maps).

### Deep-link receiver [carried]

```js
window.__oros<App>Open = function (id, ymd) { /* navigate; guard deleted ids */ };
// Boot: read sessionStorage "oros-<app>-open", remove it, invoke the receiver.
```

### Universal search provider (2026-10-09)

The menu's search field (A74) also searches the apps' own data. `search.js` (root, shell core, unit-tested in node) finds and ranks; `shell.js` draws ("In your data" under the app list, groups per app, 3 hits then "All (n)", at most 50 per app). Every app with user text ships a provider:

```js
// <app>/search.js — declared in apps.json as "search": "search.js";
// the shell loads it on the FIRST search, never at boot.
(function (root) {
  var PROVIDER = {
    id: "<app id>", keys: ["oros-<app>-data"],
    // ctx = { q, words, fold, lang, limit, readJSON(key) }
    search: function (ctx) { return [{ id, title, text, when, target }]; },  // or a Promise
    open: function (target, win) { /* optional: an existing bridge */ }
  };
  if (typeof module !== "undefined" && module.exports) module.exports = PROVIDER;
  if (root && root.document) {
    var list = root.orosSearchProviders = root.orosSearchProviders || [];
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) if (list[i] && list[i].id === PROVIDER.id) return;
    list.push(PROVIDER);
  }
})(typeof window !== "undefined" ? window : globalThis);
```

- READ-ONLY: never `setItem`, never sync, never `innerHTML`; skip tombstones, trash, archived and hidden items. `title` and `text` are plain text (HTML bodies → text in an inert document, as Writer's provider does). `when` = ms, shown as a date and used for ties: give it only when the date means something to the user (due date, event day, last edit).
- `ctx.readJSON` parses once per stored string; ranking and matching are the shell's (fold: case/accents/ς; every word must match; title prefix > title word > title > text; ties → newest). A provider that throws or answers after 1 s is skipped for that search.
- Opening: without `open`, the shell calls the generic deep link `window.__orosOpenAt(appId, target)`. App running → `contentWindow.__orosOpenAt(target)`; closed → sessionStorage `oros-open-at` = `{ app, target }`, and the app takes it at boot with `window.parent.__orosTakeTarget("<id>")`. A receiver ignores unknown ids and does nothing while one of its dialogs is open (unsaved edits win).
- Per-app on/off switches: menu → Search → "Search in", device-local `oros-search-prefs` `{ off: {id: true}, on: {id: true} }`. An app whose data is sensitive sets `"searchOff": true` in `apps.json`: it starts switched off (opt-in).
- Providers (phase 1, 2026-10-09): Notes (pages), Contacts (name; company, phones, e-mails, addresses, note), To-Do (lists + tasks), Calendar (events; next occurrence of a series, walk mirrors `eachOccurrence`), Kanban (cards; archived boards skipped), Bookmarks, Writer (documents), Files (names only, walked through `orosFS.ls`, capped at 3,000 entries / depth 12, refreshed at most every 10 s). Contacts, Calendar and Kanban open through their existing bridges; Notes, To-Do (now down to the task), Bookmarks, Writer and Files gained `__orosOpenAt` receivers.
- Shortcut: Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F opens the menu with the cursor in the field (from inside an app too).
