### Shortcut forwarding (Contract Β, capture phase) [re-verified]

```js
document.addEventListener("keydown", function (e) {
  if (!(e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey) || !e.altKey || !e.shiftKey) return;
  var p = null; try { p = window.parent; } catch (err) { return; }
  if (!(p && p !== window && p.orosShortcuts &&
        typeof p.orosShortcuts.handle === "function")) return;
  if (p.orosShortcuts.handle(e)) e.stopPropagation();
}, true);
```

App-local shortcuts match `e.code` (`KeyS`, `KeyF`, …), never `e.key`, and skip Ctrl+Alt+Shift (shell territory).

### Merge engine shape [re-verified in Writer]

```js
function newer(a, b, key) {              // symmetric pick (R5)
  var k = key || "mtime";
  var ma = (a && Number(a[k])) || 0, mb = (b && Number(b[k])) || 0;
  if (ma !== mb) return ma > mb ? a : b;
  return String(JSON.stringify(a)) >= String(JSON.stringify(b)) ? a : b;
}
```

- Union by id with sorted output.
- Tombstones: max-ts union, deduped and sorted.
- An entity is alive if its mtime > the tombstone ts.
- Column/order values: the side with the larger om donates positions.
- Strict normalizers DROP invalid rows.

### Lazy entity materialization (R28) [Writer]

```js
function ensureDoc() {
  var cur = activeDoc();
  if (cur && !cur.del) return cur;
  var d = createDoc({ silent: true, keepEditor: true });  // no re-render, caret kept
  dirty = true; flushSave();                              // capture what is on the page
  return d;
}
```

### mtime discipline (R27) [Writer]

```js
// flushSave(): stamp ONLY if the content really changed
var html = editorHTMLForSave();
if (html !== doc.html) { doc.html = html; doc.mtime = Date.now(); }
// field edits stamp at the mutation site:
function markDoc(doc) { if (doc) doc.mtime = Date.now(); scheduleSave(); }
```

### Import sanitizer (inert document) [Writer]

Allow-list thinking; remove these elements:

- `script`, `style`, `iframe`, `frame`, `frameset`, `object`, `embed`
- `noscript`, `link`, `meta`, `base`, `template`
- `form`, `input`, `button`, `textarea`, `select`
- `svg`, `math`

Remove these attributes:

- every `on*` handler, plus `srcdoc` and `formaction`;
- `href`/`src`/`action`/`data` whose control-char-stripped value starts with `javascript:`, `vbscript:` or `data:text/html`.

Parse with `document.implementation.createHTMLDocument('')`; never with a live element.

### Dismissable menus (per-instance listeners)

- Never leave `{once:true}` document listeners behind for a reusable menu: a stale one closes the NEXT menu instantly ("works every other time").
- Use one `AbortController` per menu instance; `close()` calls `abort()`.

### Dialogs [carried + Writer]

- Native `<dialog>` + `showModal()`; outside-click + Esc; null-guarded `close` listeners; remove the node on close.
- Themed confirm/prompt return Promises (`wConfirm(msg, {danger, ok})`, `wPrompt(title, value)`).
- A zero-edit close must not stamp mtime.

### i18n in an app [carried + Writer]

```js
const STRINGS = { en: { ... }, el: { ... } };          // same key set in both packs
function t(key) { return (STRINGS[appLang()] || STRINGS.en)[key] || STRINGS.en[key] || key; }
```

Escape user text with `esc()` before `innerHTML`, and use `escAttr()` in attributes. Keep key parity EN↔EL; a quick script that diffs the key sets and greps `t('…')` / `data-i18n` usages catches missing keys (Writer had one).

**Greek coverage (2026-10-14, Chris: "some users speak no English at all").** `tests/i18n.test.js` scans every `{ en: {…}, el: {…} }` table (and keys added later as `X.en["k"] = …`) in the shell and the apps: every English key must have a Greek string, and a Greek string may not be a copy of an English sentence; every `help.en.txt` / help topic needs a Greek page. Word lists and `maps/presets-data.js` are skipped. Accessible names count as text: an `aria-label`, `title` or `placeholder` written in the HTML is a placeholder that JS must translate (`data-i18n-aria="key"` / `data-i18n-title` / `data-i18n-ph`), and so are labels set by a library (Leaflet zoom and layer controls take `t()` strings). Prefer a plain Greek word over an English loanword when one exists (πίνακας, not board; έργο, not project); product and brand names stay as they are. The shell sets `#app-frame`'s `title` to the running app's name and relabels the sync button on every language change (`applyLang`).

### Form rebuild discipline (buildCapture) [carried]

Read input values + scrollTop BEFORE `innerHTML=""`, rebuild, then restore.

### File dialogs (R33) [log]

- **Helpers.** `dialogHost()` looks up `window.orosDialog`, then `window.parent.orosDialog`, inside try/catch, and returns `null` when the app runs standalone. `localPickFile()` (one-shot hidden input) exists only in apps that import files. **Reference implementation: `bookmarks.js`.** Copy it from the file; it is not quoted here because the file was not on the table for this revision.
- **Funnel first.** When an app exports through one function (`downloadBlob`), migrate that function once instead of every call site (Writer: one patch covered 8 formats).
- **Library bypass.** A library's own download path skips the funnel: jsPDF `doc.save()` → `doc.output("blob")` → funnel (Cycle, Mood, Writer).
- **Transient activation.** A click-triggered synchronous export opens the native picker legally. An async exporter (PDF: vendor load + font fetch) may outlast the activation; `dialogs.js` then falls back to download. Where it matters, pre-warm the vendors when the export dialog opens (Writer).
- **Visible file inputs** that are part of a form: route the click in the capture phase to `openFile`, and keep the input as the standalone fallback. Reset `input.value = ""` after reading so the same file can be picked again.
- **Out of scope by design:** OS drag & drop, clipboard paste, and the shell backup-folder subsystem (§5d: a persistent folder handle with its own permission lifecycle).
- **Zero-touch at the close of Wave 2** (no user-file I/O, so no helper, R36): habits, maps, minimalism, prompter, radio, storage, time, astro, todo, weather, `fs.js`, `pet.js`.

### App-level import / restore [log, Contacts + Kanban]

- A restore is a merge, never an overwrite: send the parsed file through the app's own sync merge (`mergeFn`, landing like a pull), then persist and mark dirty.
- An import from a foreign format fills empty fields and unions by key. It never replaces a value the user curated.
- Foreign entities get deterministic prefixed ids (`imp-k-`, `imp-t-`), so a re-import is idempotent and two devices converge. They arrive as NEW entities with a fresh mtime; existing ones are not touched. Take a real Undo snapshot first.
- Never guess a foreign format: get a real export sample first (Mantra).

### Cross-app "new entry" bridge: Maps → Calendar (BR-W8) [log]

Rule ids are kept as recorded.

- **BR-W8-1 · Contract.** `window.parent.__orosOpenCalendarNew({ date, title?, location?, start?, note? })`. `date` is mandatory `"YYYY-MM-DD"` (strict regex guard in `shell.js`); `start` is 24h `"HH:MM"`. The rest are optional strings, truncated by the receiver (location 150, note 500). The receiver (`__orosCalendarNew` in calendar.js) also reads `end`, `dateEnd` and, since Calendar wave 8, `allDay: true` and `recur` (normalised with `normRecur`); the Calendar's own quick add and "Copy to my calendar" use these.
- **BR-W8-2 · Staging key.** sessionStorage `oros-cal-new`, NOT `oros-cal-pending` (reserved for event deep links). Device-local, never synced, never exported. The original note's remark about the factory reset contradicts itself (A10).
- **BR-W8-3 · One receiver.** `window.__orosCalendarNew` is defined inside `calendar.js` and has exactly two entries: a live push from the shell (`state.running === "calendar"`) and boot-time consumption of the staged payload (250 ms delay). Any new entry path goes through it.
- **BR-W8-4 · One-shot take.** Read, then remove. A stale app bundle without the receiver ignores the payload; nothing breaks.
- **BR-W8-5 · Standalone.** `/calendar/?new={urlencoded JSON}`, consumed at boot (400 ms delay). A future app handing a new entry to a standalone Calendar reuses this parameter.
- **BR-W8-6 · A bridged payload is a PREFILL, not data.** Nothing reaches the slice (no `markDirty`, no sync traffic) until the user saves in the New Event dialog. Mandatory for any future bridge of this shape.
- **BR-W8-7 · Reverse direction.** Calendar locations are clickable in Day (`.ev-loc`), Week (`.wk-ev-loc`) and Search (`.res-loc`), each with `evt.stopPropagation()`, all through the single `openInMaps()` → `window.parent.__orosOpenMapsQuery(query, label)`. A new view extends `openInMaps()`; it does not add a fourth path.
- **BR-W8-8 · Availability.** "Send to Calendar" is gated by `routeTo && lastSteps.length`. Since Maps Dose 1 the button is still JS-appended at `wire()` time, has id `route-cal`, sits before `#nav-start` and is styled by `maps.css`.
- **BR-W8-9 · Payload.** Title "Route to {dest}" / «Διαδρομή προς {προορισμός}» (from `maps.js`'s own `LANG`, not `window.t`); location = destination name; start = current local time; note = distance · duration · transport mode.

### Cross-app "new entry" bridge: any app → Budget (BR-B1)

Owner: Budget (`budget/`). Senders (Garage, Split, …) never edit `budget/`. Same shape as BR-W8.

- **BR-B1-1 · Contract.** `window.parent.__orosOpenBudgetNew({ k, a, d?, n?, c?, src? })` → `true` (accepted: Budget opened or got the push) or `false` (rejected, nothing opens; also `false` when Budget is not installed).
  - `k`: `"o"` expense | `"i"` income (required).
  - `a`: integer cents, `0 < a ≤ 100000000000` (required). Convert once at the edge, `Math.round(x * 100)`.
  - `d`: `"YYYY-MM-DD"`, a real date (optional; default today on the device).
  - `n`: note, plain text; Budget trims it and keeps 140 chars.
  - `c`: category id hint, language-free, one of the ready ids `o-groc o-eat o-bills o-home o-trans o-health o-fun o-cloth o-gift o-other i-salary i-free i-gift i-other`. Used only if it still exists and is of kind `k`; else Budget's usual default. Never a name or a user's own id.
  - `src`: sender app id `[a-z0-9]{1,20}`; the form shows "From {app}" / «Από: {app}» with the name from the shell's `app.<id>` string.
- **BR-B1-2 · Validation.** The shell checks kind, amount and date strictly and hands over a fresh plain copy of the known fields only. Budget checks again with `normPrefill()` (tested in `tests/budget.test.js`).
- **BR-B1-3 · One receiver.** `window.__orosBudgetNew` in `budget.js`, two entries: a live push when Budget is the running app, and the one-shot take of sessionStorage `oros-budget-new` at boot (read, then remove; device-local, never synced, never exported). Standalone: `/budget/?new={urlencoded JSON}`; the parameter is removed from the address after it is read.
- **BR-B1-4 · A PREFILL, not data (BR-W8-6).** The New entry form opens filled in, focus on Save. Nothing reaches the slice, sync or limit notifications until the user saves; Cancel leaves no trace. Every text is rendered with `textContent`.
- **BR-B1-5 · Senders.** Show the button ("Add to Budget" / «Προσθήκη στα Έσοδα & Έξοδα») only when `typeof window.parent.__orosOpenBudgetNew === "function"`, and call it only from that explicit button: there is no duplicate guard, the user confirms each entry. Senders include Pet Health Book (visit editor "Add to Budget", k "o", c "o-health", note "{pet}: {reason}"; since 0.55.00).

### Cross-app "open in Spreadsheet": any app → a new sheet (BR-S1)

Owner: Spreadsheet (`spreadsheet/`). First sender: Budget (Export → "Open in Spreadsheet").

- **BR-S1-1 · Contract.** `window.parent.__orosOpenAt("spreadsheet", { newSheet: { name, rows, sum? } })` through the generic deep link (`__orosOpenAt` / `__orosTakeTarget`, staged in sessionStorage `oros-open-at`). `rows` = array of rows, row 1 = heading; a cell is a finite number, a string or null/"". `sum` = 0-based columns that get `=SUM(…)` under the last row.
- **BR-S1-2 · Always a NEW sheet**, never overwrites; capped at 500 rows × 64 columns (the sender caps first and says so). `name` goes through `xlSafeName`.
- **BR-S1-3 · No formulas from the sender.** A string cell is plain text; one starting with `= + - @` gets a leading apostrophe. The only formulas are the receiver's own `SUM`s.
- **BR-S1-4 · Receiver.** `sheetFromTable()` in `spreadsheet.js`: live push via `window.__orosOpenAt(target)`, boot take via `takeTarget()`. It marks the slice dirty like any import (it is user data from then on).

### Budget recurring entries in the Calendar (BR-B2)

Owner: Budget (`budget/feed.js`). Reader: Calendar (chip "Budget" / «Προϋπολογισμός», `lbl-feed-budget`, emerald `#2bb673`).

- **BR-B2-1 · One file, no storage.** `budget/feed.js` (`window.OrosBudgetFeed`: `occurrences`, `rowsOn(data, ymd, today, lang)`) is pure and only reads `oros-budget-data`; `calendar/index.html` loads it before `calendar.js`. Rows are built on render (micro-cached ~1s like the other feeds), never stored or synced.
- **BR-B2-2 · Same days as Budget.** `occurrences()` in `feed.js` is a copy of the one in `budget.js` (monthly/yearly keep the first date's day, clamped to the month's end; weekly every 7 days; both ends inclusive), and its `SEED_NAMES` is a copy too. `tests/budget-feed.test.js` fails if either drifts: change both together.
- **BR-B2-3 · What shows.** Only today and later (earlier occurrences are real entries in Budget by then). A deleted recurring entry (`rec:<id>` tombstone) or a deleted occurrence (`tx:<recTxId>` tombstone) shows nothing; the end date is respected. Title = the note, else the category name, then the signed amount in Budget's currency (`−500,00 €` / `+1.200,50 €`), rendered with `textContent`.
- **BR-B2-4 · Click-through.** `window.parent.__orosOpenAt("budget", { rec: id })`. Receiver `openTarget()` in `budget.js` (live push via `window.__orosOpenAt`, boot take via `takeTarget()`): closes an open dialog, switches to the Recurring tab and opens that entry; a deleted one gives the toast "This recurring entry was deleted". It also takes `{ tx: id }` (the entry on its month), the target universal search uses.

### Cross-app "new quote" bridge: any app → Quote (BR-Q1)

Owner: Quote (`quote/`). First sender: Timesheet (report "Create quote"). Same shape as BR-W8 / BR-B1.

- **BR-Q1-1 · Contract.** `window.parent.__orosOpenQuoteNew({ items, cur?, client?, notes? })` → `true` (Quote opened or got the push) or `false` (rejected, nothing opens; also `false` when Quote is not installed).
  - `items`: 1–50 lines `{ d, q, p }`: `d` description (plain text, ≤ 200 chars), `q` quantity `0 < q ≤ 100000`, `p` unit price in currency units (not cents) `0 ≤ p ≤ 10000000`; both rounded to 2 decimals.
  - `cur`: any ISO 4217 code, three capital letters (`/^[A-Z]{3}$/`; wave 46 — before, `"EUR"` | `"USD"` only). Anything else rejects the call. Senders (Timesheet, Stock, CRM) pass their own currency as it is; Assistant's `quote` kind takes the same rule (wave 46 follow-up).
  - `client`: client name (≤ 80 chars), matched case-insensitively against Quote's clients.
  - `notes`: plain text, ≤ 500 chars.
  - Control characters other than tab and newline are stripped from every text.
- **BR-Q1-2 · One receiver.** `window.__orosQuoteNew` in `quote.js`: a live push when Quote is running, and the one-shot take of sessionStorage `oros-quote-new` at boot (read, then remove; device-local, never synced, never exported; taken before `oros-quote-open`).
- **BR-Q1-3 · A PREFILL, not data (BR-W8-6).** A new draft opens on the Create tab with the lines (VAT = Quote's default), currency and client filled in. Nothing is saved until the user presses Save. If the current unsaved draft has content (client, notes, or a line with text or price), a confirm ("Replace the unsaved draft…?") comes first; Cancel leaves the draft as it was. An unknown client opens the New client dialog with the name filled in; the client exists only if the user saves that dialog. Every text is rendered as an input value / `textContent`.
- **BR-Q1-4 · Timesheet sender.** Button `#rep-quote`, shown only when `typeof window.parent.__orosOpenQuoteNew === "function"`. `core.quoteLines()` uses the report's period and client/project/invoiced filters, billable time only, grouped by project: `d` = "Project · period" (`fmtRange`), `q` = billable hours (rounding prefs applied), `p` = the project's hourly rate. Lines with no billable time are dropped; `client` is sent only when every line belongs to one client. Timesheet's currency goes along whatever it is (wave 46). Sending does not mark entries invoiced (that stays the report's own button).

### Quote wave 46: currencies, email with PDF, acceptance by link (BR-Q-ACC)
- **Currencies.** `quote/core.js` (v1.2.0) `curOk`, `currencyList` (common codes, then `Intl.supportedValuesOf("currency")`), `fmtMoney(n, cur, lang, codeOnly)` (Intl, en-GB / el-GR, the currency's own decimals), `curDigits`, `convert(amount, rate, to)`. A stored `q.currency` that isn't three capital letters loads as EUR; every valid code is kept (old EUR/USD quotes load unchanged). The PDF uses symbols when its Noto font is in, else codes.
- **Total in another currency** (display only): device-local `oros-quote-local.convTo`; rates from the shared ECB helper `UnitsCore.fetchLatest` / `crossRate` and its cache (quote/index.html loads ../units/core.js); no fetcher of its own. Never stored on the quote.
- **Email with PDF.** "Send via email" builds the PDF (`exportPdf(onBlob)`) and opens Mail compose `__orosOpenAt("mail", {compose: {to, subject, body, attach: [{name, type: "application/pdf", b64}]}})` when Mail has an account on the device (`oros-mail-data`); else mailto, with a toast that the PDF must be attached by hand. relay/ untouched.
- **BR-Q-ACC (acceptance by link, no server).** Pure rules in `quote/accept-core.js` (`OrosQuoteAccept`). Offer link `quote/accept.html#q1.<base64url(deflate-raw(JSON))>` (`q0.` = plain JSON without CompressionStream; ≤ 32 768 chars, ≤ 256 KB inflated); the client page (accept.html / accept.js / accept.css, renders with textContent only, keeps inheritPalette / watchPalette) shows the snapshot and takes a typed name (+ checkbox, optional note ≤ 500). Answer link `quote/#acc=a1.<base64url(JSON {i, t, h, n, at, m?})>`; quote/index.html forwards `#acc=` to the shell (`?open=quote&app-at=`), the app takes it at boot, or the user pastes it in "Record acceptance".
  - On send the quote gets `q.share = {tok (128-bit random, base64url), h (SHA-256 hex of the canonical snapshot, token inside), at, f, fe}` — synced with the quote. A resend with an unchanged snapshot reuses the same token (same link); a changed quote gets a new token, so answers to older links read "stale".
  - `verify(q, reply)`: "ok" only when `reply.t === q.share.tok` AND `reply.h === q.share.h`; "tampered" when the token matches but the hash doesn't; "stale" for an older token; "none" when the quote was never sent. On "ok" the user confirms "Mark as accepted": `q.status = "accepted"`, `q.acc = {n, at, h, m?}`, then "Make invoice" (existing Invoices bridge).
  - Honest scope (also in help Limits): this is integrity against an edited link, not authentication. The hash is computable by anyone holding the offer link, so such a person could forge an answer; the name is typed, not verified. It is not an electronic signature. Old quotes without `share` / `acc` load unchanged; older devices keep the extra fields through their merge (unknown fields pass through the quote record).
- Tests: `tests/quote-wave46.test.js`.

### Cross-app "send to To-Do" bridge: any app → To-Do list (BR-TD-ADD)

Owner: To-Do (`todo/`, section 13 of `todo.js`). First sender: Meal Planner (Shopping "To To-Do"). Planned senders: Chore Wheel (one chore), Travel (a packing list as a new list). No new shell code: it rides the generic deep link `__orosOpenAt` / `__orosTakeTarget`.

- **BR-TD-ADD-1 · Contract.** `window.parent.__orosOpenAt("todo", { addItems: { list?, newList?, from?, items } })`. Senders show their button only when `typeof window.parent.__orosOpenAt === "function"`.
  - `items`: 1–200 `{ text, note? }`; `text` one line, ≤ 300 chars; `note` (To-Do's Notes field) keeps newlines, ≤ 1000 chars. Extra items are dropped; items whose text normalizes the same (case, accents, punctuation, as To-Do search) are sent once.
  - `list`: a To-Do list id to suggest (e.g. `tdl-groceries`, the fixed seed id of Groceries / Ψώνια). Unknown → the `newList` option if given, else the open list.
  - `newList`: a name (≤ 60 chars) offered as "New list: …" in the list picker; the list is created only when the user adds.
  - `from`: the sending app's name in the user's language (≤ 60 chars), shown as "From …".
  - Control characters (and U+2028/2029) are replaced by spaces in every text; everything is shown with `textContent`. A payload with no usable item is ignored (To-Do just opens).
- **BR-TD-ADD-2 · A PREFILL, not data (BR-W8-6).** To-Do opens the dialog `#todo-add`: list picker, every item ticked, except items already OPEN (not done) in the chosen list, which start unticked with "already on the list" (re-checked when the list changes; a tick the user changed stays). Nothing touches `oros-todo-data` until "Add N"; Cancel leaves no trace. Add puts the ticked items at the top of the list in payload order (one `list.om` stamp, items fully stamped), switches to that list and clears search/filters. The sender never writes To-Do's slice (one writer per slice).
- **BR-TD-ADD-3 · Meal Planner sender.** Button `#sh-todo` on the Shopping tab sends the unticked items of the list on screen (the week shown, "From today" applied): `text` = "qty name" as in Copy, `note` = "for <recipes>", `list` = `tdl-groceries`. Ticks in Meal Planner are not changed.
- **BR-TD-ADD-4 · Chore Wheel sender.** "Send to To-Do" in a chore's actions dialog (only while it is open, not done or skipped): one item, `text` = icon + chore name, `note` = "Chore Wheel · <day or range>" (+ " · <member>" when it is someone else's), no `list` (To-Do's open list). The chore's "done" stays in Chore Wheel only; nothing syncs back.
- **BR-TD-ADD-5 · Travel sender (0.60.02, #133).** Trip menu items "Send "Before I leave" to To-Do" and "Send "Still to pack" to To-Do", shown only when the bridge exists and the list has open items: `newList` = "<trip> · before I leave" / "<trip> · to pack" (≤ 60 chars), `from` = Travel, `items` = the open (not done) packing items of the `@before` group or of all other groups (≤ 200): `text` = name or "n × name" when qty > 1, `note` = who · note. A copy, not a live link; Travel data is not changed.
- **BR-TD-ADD-6 · Garage sender (0.61.02, #140).** "→ To-Do" in the head of Overview's "Coming up" sends every row shown there (alerts first, then the next renewals / service items, up to 5); a "To-Do" button in the renewal and service-plan editors sends that one. No `list` (To-Do's open list), `from` = Garage / Γκαράζ. `text`: KTEO "Book the KTEO test · <vehicle>", other renewals "Renew <what> · <vehicle>", service "Book a service: <item> · <vehicle>", tyres "Replace tyres: <set> · <vehicle>". `note` = "Garage · expires <date>" (or the due date / km) · provider · reference · plate. Shown only when `__orosOpenAt` exists. Garage data is not changed.

### Today summary: apps → Today (BR-TODAY)

- **BR-TODAY-1 · Provider.** An app with something dated ships `<app>/today.js` and names it in apps.json: `"today": "today.js"` (or a list of at most 4 files of that folder, loaded in order). The shell (`today/host.js`) loads it the first time a summary is built. The file pushes ONE object onto `window.orosTodayProviders`: `{ id, keys: [storage keys it reads], collect(ctx) → [row] | Promise, open?(target, win) }`; under Node it is `module.exports` (tests/today.test.js runs every provider against its app's real core).
- **BR-TODAY-2 · Rows.** `{ id, due: "YYYY-MM-DD"|null, time: "HH:MM"|null, title, text, kind: "task"|"event"|"info", target }`. `today/agg.js` cleans them (plain text, title ≤ 160, text ≤ 240, target JSON ≤ 500 chars) and groups them: info lines (today only), Overdue (tasks only; a past event is gone, not late), Today (timed first), Coming up (next 3 days). At most 50 rows of one app per group, the rest is a count.
- **BR-TODAY-3 · Read-only.** A provider never writes storage, never talks to sync, never fetches. `ctx = { today, horizon, now, lang, readJSON(key), readRaw(key), addDays, diff }`. The date logic stays in the app's own core. A provider that throws or answers after 1 s is left out of that summary.
- **BR-TODAY-4 · The notice.** One `orosNotifs.emit({ ns: "today", key: "day-<ymd>", type: "reminder", deepLink: "today:<ymd>" })` a day, numbers only, only when Overdue + Today > 0. Built from the start hour (slice `hour`, default 6, 0–12), after the unlock and the first sync merge (`settled`: no cloud → at once; locked → never; else after a pull, 2 min after a failure / offline boot, 10 min with no answer). Device-local `oros-today-local {last, sent}` stops a second build; the inbox dedup (ns:key) stops a second device. An empty day retries after 30 min or after new synced data.
- **BR-TODAY-5 · Morning reminders.** `orosToday.absorbs(ns)` (shell `todayAbsorbs`) keeps the shell's own morning reminders of the apps in the summary quiet (calendar name days, garage, petcare (doses still ring), plants, chores, weather briefing; since wave 2 also todo and quote; since wave 4 minimalism) when the "quiet" setting is on: quiet once today's notice is in the inbox; held while it is being built (≤ 10 min after boot); released on an empty day, with Today off, the app switched off, or Today not registered.
- **BR-TODAY-6 · Assistant.** The row button only pre-fills `__orosOpenAt("assistant", {ask})` (≤ 2000 chars) and shows only when the Assistant is set up and `OrosAssistCore.permFor` gives "ask" or "always" for that app. NEVER_APPS unchanged, so Mail's lines (wave 3) never get the button; inside Mail the existing Mail → Assistant bridge works per message.
- **BR-TODAY-7 · Settings slice "today"** (`oros-today-data`, registered with a null storage key, always live in the shell): `{ ver, on, hour, absorb, apps: { id: {v, m} } }`, each field `{v, m}`, newest m wins, a tie goes to the larger JSON (R5), canonical order (R26), stamped only on a real change (R27). Cycle and Mood are off by default (sensitive); every app can be switched either way (Chris 2026-10-11).
- **BR-TODAY-8 · Wave 2 shared cores (one copy each).** `calendar/occur.js` (OrosCalOccur: eachOccurrence, occursOn, eventsOn) replaces the Calendar's and the shell's `calRemEachOccurrence` copies; `todo/core.js` (OrosTodoCore: openDue, dueOn, dueSummary) serves the shell's `todoCheckTick` and the Calendar's To-Do feed; `quote/core.js` (OrosQuoteCore: dueQuotes, clientName) serves `quoteCheckTick`; `kanban/core.js` (OrosKanbanCore: dueCards, `skipLast` leaves out each board's last column for Today; the Calendar still shows every column); `contacts/dates.js` (OrosContactDates: eventsOn, displayName) serves the Calendar's Contacts feed. Locked by golden tests (tests/today-wave2.test.js). Two intended fixes: a 29 February date shows on 28 February in other years; a sent/accepted quote without a due date no longer counts as due.
- **BR-TODAY-9 · "Done".** A row may carry `done` (small JSON). The Today tab shows a tick that only calls `__orosOpenAt(app, {done})`; the app writes with its own code: To-Do `{done:{list,item}}` → `setDone` (the checkbox's function; recurring tasks reopen with their next date), Plant Care `{done:{plant,kind}}` → `logTask` (Undo in its toast). Gone / already done → a note, nothing written. Only To-Do, Plant Care and CRM offer it.
- **BR-TODAY-10 · Wave 3 providers and shared rules.** `habits/core.js` (OrosHabitsCore: schedIdx Monday = 0, isScheduledOn, isDone, dueOn) serves habits.js and the Calendar's Habits feed; `fitness/core.js` gains OrosFitnessCore (plannedOn = the Train tab's "Today", doneOn = a finished workout of that program day); `OrosMealsCore.planByDay` serves the Calendar's Meals feed; `OrosHealthCore.timesOn(d, now)` gives today's reminder times with `done` (a reading of that kind from 1 h before the time until 1 h before the next time of that kind, or the day's end). Golden tests: tests/today-wave3.test.js. Providers: Habits (scheduled today, not ticked; flexible habits never due), Workouts (`{train:true}` → Train tab), Health (open reminder times, `__orosOpenHealth(kind)`), Budget (`OrosBudgetFeed.rowsOn`, today + 3 days, `{rec}`), Meal Planner (info lines, `{day}`), Mail (info lines: unread count of each living account's INBOX from IndexedDB `oros-mail` store `folders` (Mail's own last refresh, with its time), opened without a version and closed at once; no relay, no password, no sender or subject; `__orosOpenAt("mail", {acct, folder})` opens that folder). Info (top) lines open their app too. Nothing new is absorbed: the Health hour reminders still ring.
- **BR-TODAY-11 · Wave 4 providers and shared rules.** `cycle/core.js` (OrosCycleCore: avgCycleLen, avgPeriodLen, nextPrediction, dueIn = the reminder's "≤ 2 days or past") serves cycle.js and the shell's closed-app `cycleShellCheck` (its copy of the math is gone; strings stay); `mood/core.js` (OrosMoodCore: hasAny, hasOn; an entry without a valid time no longer counts as today) serves `moodCheckInTick`; `minimalism/core.js` (OrosMinimalismCore: hasAny, engagedOn, remindHour) serves `minimalismCheckTick`, which is now absorbed (BR-TODAY-5); `OrosNamedays.petBirthday(pet, ymd)` serves the Calendar's pet feed. The shell loads the three new cores. Golden tests: tests/today-wave4.test.js. Providers: Cycle (expected start in the horizon as an event; late ≤ 14 days as a top line; `__orosOpenCycle(ymd)`), Mood (check-in task while nothing is logged today, once the app was used; `__orosOpenMood("checkin")`), Minimalism (task while today's proposal is neither done nor skipped; the text stays in content.js; `__orosOpenMinimalism(ymd)`), Family Tree (death anniversaries, `{person}`), Moon & Sky (OrosSkyCore.feedFor, today's as top lines, `{date}`), Calendar += the screen pet's birthday (respects the device-local pet Calendar opt-out; `__orosOpenPet(null)`). Cycle and Mood stay off by default (BR-TODAY-7).
- **BR-TODAY-12 · Sticky Notes (1.12.00).** `stickies/today.js`: one task row per open ring (late ones Overdue), repeating rings up to the horizon, max 8 rounds; target opens through `__orosOpenStickies(id)`. Reads `oros-stickies-data` only.
- **BR-TODAY-13 · Widgets (wave 48).** `today/layout.js` (`OrosTodayLayout`, pure, Node-tested in `tests/today-layout.test.js`): catalogue `top` (the info lines), `overdue`, `today`, `soon` (the old sections), `clock`, `weather`, `water`, `habits`, `events`, `todos`; kind `list` | `tile`; sizes `small` | `wide` (`top` wide only). Layout `{ v: 1, items: [{ id, size }] }` in **device-local** `localStorage["oros-today-layout"]` (R10: a phone and a laptop want different screens; never in the slice `today`; removed when equal to the default). `norm` drops unknown ids (a newer version's), doubles and bad sizes; not an object / no `items` → the default (`top, overdue, today, soon`, exactly the pre-wave screen); an empty list is kept. `distribute(groups, ids)` gives each widget its parts `[{ late? | today? | day, rows, more }]`; a row goes to ONE widget: with `weather` / `water` on the screen their app's info line leaves `top`, `habits` takes Habits rows of overdue + today (later days stay in `soon`), `events` takes Calendar rows of kind `event` (Calendar's info lines and tasks stay), `todos` takes To-Do rows; the "and N more" counts follow. "Nothing for today" shows in the `today` slot (else `overdue`) when no widget has a late or today row. UI: toolbar `#edit-btn` (Customise / Done, `aria-pressed`): edit cards with a drag handle (pointer events followed on the document, `touch-action: none` on the handle, edge auto-scroll; works with mouse and touch), up / down buttons (touch + keyboard), size toggle, remove; "Add a widget" lists `hidden()`; "Back to the standard layout". Moves are announced in `#live`. Grid: two columns at every width; small tiles share a row even at 360 px, small lists take one column from 900 px. Clock: `hour12: false`, seconds and the long date when wide.

### File handover: .ics → Calendar, .vcf → Contacts (BR-FILE-IMPORT)

- **Contract.** `__orosOpenAt("calendar", { importIcs: { name, text } })` and `__orosOpenAt("contacts", { importVcf: { name, text } })` through the generic deep link (`__orosOpenAt` / `__orosTakeTarget`). `text` = the file's text, `name` = its file name (shown only, `textContent`). The sender (the shell's file handlers / share target) reads the File, refuses anything over 5 MB and passes `file.text()`; the receivers refuse over 5 M characters too.
- **Never silent.** Both receivers parse first and show a themed dialog (file name + counts); nothing is written until Import. Cancel / Esc drops the parsed data.
- **Calendar.** `calendar/ics.js` (`window.OrosIcs.parse`, pure, Node-tested in `tests/calendar-ics.test.js`) maps an RFC 5545 subset to the Calendar's event shape: UTC / floating times converted to local time; a DTSTART TZID that Intl knows (and is not UTC or the device zone) is kept as the event's `tz` with its wall times (EXDATE/UNTIL/RECURRENCE-ID resolved in that zone); all-day DTEND exclusive; RRULE through `OCC.fromRrule` (any INTERVAL, weekly BYDAY lists, monthly BYMONTHDAY = start day, BYDAY `nWD` / `-1WD` or BYDAY+BYSETPOS single position, yearly with BYMONTH, the clamp form `BYMONTHDAY=28..31;BYSETPOS=-1`, UNTIL or COUNT, WKST), anything richer (several month days, several positions, BYWEEKNO/BYYEARDAY, sub-daily) imports its first date and is counted as "simplified" (never extra occurrences); EXDATE; RECURRENCE-ID becomes its own event plus an excluded date on the series; first VALARM equal to a reminder preset; STATUS:CANCELLED skipped; first CATEGORIES matched to an existing label by name (labels are never created). Ids: UID `<id>@oros.calendar` (our export) → `<id>`, any other UID → `ics-` + 64-bit FNV hash, so a re-import updates instead of duplicating. Compared with the store: new / updated (content differs) / unchanged; only new and updated are written, with a fresh mtime (they sync and win over an older copy or tombstone like an edit). At most 5000 events per file. The Import button (next to Export) uses the same path.
- **Contacts.** Same vCard path as the Import button: the import review (below), which names the file.
- **Contacts "From phone"** (Contact Picker API, Chrome on Android only; the button stays hidden elsewhere): the person picks contacts in the system sheet, only those reach the page (name, phones, emails, addresses when offered), then the same import review.

### Contacts: import review and "From an account" (BR-CT-IMPORT)

- **One review for every import** (vCard / CSV file, From phone, BR-FILE-IMPORT, From an account). `contacts/importplan.js` (`OrosContactsImport`, pure, Node-tested in `tests/contacts-import.test.js`): `plan(local, incoming, labels)` folds duplicates inside the import first, then matches each incoming contact against this device's contacts by e-mail, else phone (`samePhone`: digits, a leading 00 dropped, the shorter number ≥ 8 digits may be the tail of the longer, so +30 210… = 210…), else first + last name (accent/case folded); one local contact is claimed once. Kinds: `new` (default add), `same` (nothing to add or change; skipped, shown collapsed), `diff` (`add` = empty fields / missing rows / labels by name / photo / favourite / a year for a year-less event; `conflicts` = a one-value field that differs after folding, or a different single birthday; default merge keeping mine). A name-only match where both sides carry phones or e-mails and none is shared is `nameOnly`, default add. `apply(local, inc, "mine"|"theirs", labelIds)` returns a merged copy: fills, appends missing rows, replaces conflicts only with "theirs"; never removes anything.
- **UI.** `#rev-dlg` (Review import): source line, counts, "When a detail differs" (sets every conflicted merge at once), groups Other details / New / Already here (collapsed); per row a select (add, skip, merge keep mine, merge use imported, add as separate) and the reasons (same e-mail / phone / name, what it adds, `Field: mine → theirs`). At most 300 rows drawn per group, the rest keep their default. Import writes once (`saveState`), new contacts get a fresh id and mtime, merged ones a fresh mtime (they win the sync merge like an edit); categories resolve to labels by name (created when missing). Undo (toast, 8 s): merged contacts get their earlier copy back with a fresh mtime, added ones are tombstoned. All text through `textContent`.
- **From an account** (`contacts/accounts.js`, `OrosContactsAccounts`; button `#ct-acct`, dialog `#ac-dlg`). One-shot, browser only, no server of orOS, no secret, nothing stored. Google: OAuth 2.0 token flow (`response_type=token`, scope `contacts.readonly`, `prompt=select_account`), People API `contactGroups` (user groups → labels) and `people/me/connections` (paged, 1000 per page), token revoked at `oauth2.googleapis.com/revoke` right after the read. Microsoft: code flow + PKCE on `login.microsoftonline.com/common` (scope `Contacts.Read`, SPA redirect), Graph `/me/contacts` and every `/me/contactFolders/{id}/contacts` (`@odata.nextLink` followed only on graph.microsoft.com); no revoke call exists, the token is dropped and expires within the hour. No refresh token or offline scope is ever asked for. Caps: 60 pages, 20,000 contacts. Photos are not imported (no network imports). Mappers `fromGoogle(person, groupNames)` / `fromGraph(contact)` → the parser shape; a contact with no name is named by its first e-mail or phone; Outlook's year 1604 = no year.
- **Sign-in window.** Opened synchronously on the click (`about:blank`, then the provider URL). The provider returns to `contacts/oauth-callback.html` (+ `.js`), which clears the address bar and passes `{token|code, state, error}` on BroadcastChannel `oros-contacts-oauth` and in localStorage `oros-contacts-oauth-cb` (read and deleted at once; an unread record older than 2 min is dropped on the next load). No network calls on that page. The sign-in pages cut `window.opener` (COOP), so a closed popup is not taken as cancel; closing `#ac-dlg` cancels the wait; 10 min timeout.
- **Client ids.** `CLIENT.google` / `CLIENT.microsoft` in `accounts.js` (Google set 1.88.02, project "orOS" of Chris; Microsoft empty until registered) (Google Cloud: OAuth client "Web application", People API enabled, JavaScript origin https://useoros.online, redirect https://useoros.online/contacts/oauth-callback.html, consent screen with the sensitive scope `contacts.readonly`, which needs Google verification beyond 100 test users; Microsoft Entra: app registration for "personal Microsoft accounts and any organisation", platform Single-page application with the same redirect, delegated permission Contacts.Read). Until then a provider says "not set up yet"; anyone can register their own and enter it under "Use my own app id" (device-local, localStorage `oros-contacts-oauth`, `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` only).

### Phone bridge: orOS Contacts and Calendar in the phone (BR-PHONE v1)

- **Where.** Only inside the orOS Android app built from `android/` (TWA + native code, same package `online.useoros.twa` and signing key as the store package). Everywhere else `window.orosPhone.available()` is false and the "On this phone" buttons stay hidden.
- **Channel.** TWA postMessage (Chrome 115+): the app validates `use_as_origin` (in `.well-known/assetlinks.json`), opens a channel after each page load and posts a `MessagePort`; `phone.js` (shell, loads before `shell.js`) keeps the newest port (a relaunch opens a new channel to the same page) that has no source window (posted by the browser itself, so never a frame or another window), from any origin (browsers differ in what they put there); a port posted by the page to itself must carry this origin. The page's first `{t:"state"}` carries `o`, the origin it saw (diagnostics). The app requests one channel per page load (Chromium re-checks the origin for each request and reports it again, so answering every result loops). The app warms the browser up (`CustomTabsClient.connectAndInitialize`) before validating, since Chromium answers `validateRelationship` with false until `warmup()` was called. The app runs in the user's default browser when it supports TWAs (Chrome, Brave, Edge, Samsung Internet); Firefox does not, so another installed TWA browser is used. Messages are JSON strings. Page → app: `{t:"state"}`, `{t:"contacts"|"calendar", seq, items}`, `{t:"clear", what}`, `{t:"applied", what, refs}`. App → page also `{t:"changes", what, items}` (v2). App → page: `{t:"state", contacts, calendar: "granted"|"ask"|"denied", app}`, `{t:"done", what, seq, added, updated, removed, kept}`, `{t:"error", what, seq, msg}`.
- **orOS → phone.** The app writes an "orOS" account as its sync adapter: one raw contact per contact (`SOURCE_ID` = orOS id, `SYNC1` = row hash) and one "orOS" calendar (`_SYNC_ID` = id, `SYNC_DATA1` = hash, reminders as alerts, `EVENT_COLOR` = the label colour from the row's `color`). Unchanged rows are skipped, changed rows rebuilt, rows that left orOS deleted. Edits made in the phone apps come back (v2, below). Data leaves orOS only into this phone's own providers, never to a server; the page sends plain rows because the native side never decrypts anything.
- **Rows.** Pure `contactRows(blob)` / `eventRows(blob, tz)` / `feedRows(store, tz)` in `phone.js`, Node-tested in `tests/phone.test.js`: tombstones respected, phones/emails deduped, photo only as JPEG/PNG ≤ 70 000 base64 chars; all-day events in UTC, timed in the event's `tz` (row `tz` → `EVENT_TIMEZONE`) or the device zone; series as RRULE from `OCC.toRrule` (BYDAY lists, `-1FR`, COUNT or UNTIL) + DURATION covering the whole span, with EXDATE at instance starts; month-end and Feb 29 series use `BYMONTHDAY=…;BYSETPOS=-1` so Android clamps like the Calendar.
- **Two-way Calendar (v2).** Own events live in the writable "orOS" calendar (`CAL_ACCESS_OWNER`), feed rows (ids `f` + 16 hex) in a read-only "orOS feeds" calendar (`NAME` `orOS-feeds`). Rows Android marks `DIRTY` (added, edited, deleted, or an edited/cancelled occurrence with `ORIGINAL_SYNC_ID`) are never overwritten or removed by a snapshot; the app sends them as `{t:"changes", what:"calendar", items:[{ref:"r<rowId>", op, id, title, desc, loc, allDay, dtstart, dtend, duration, rrule, exdate, remind, orig:{id, at}, cancelled}]}` after each calendar snapshot and each `{t:"state"}` (the page sends one when it comes back on screen). `phone.js` `applyCalendarChanges(blob, items, now)` (pure, tested) applies them with `mtime = now`: upsert keeps the label of an existing event, new ones get a new id and no label, delete leaves a tombstone, an occurrence adds an exdate to the series plus (when changed) a single event with the series label; RRULE goes through `OCC.fromRrule` (rich rules kept; an unsupported one falls back to FREQ only); change rows carry no `EVENT_TIMEZONE`, so an edit of a zoned event is re-expressed in the stored `tz` (proposed Android change: add it to the change rows); reminders snap to the nearest preset. The page writes the blob, calls `orosSync.markDirty()`, makes an open Calendar re-read it (`__orosPhoneReload`), answers `{t:"applied", what, refs}` and pushes a fresh snapshot; the app then clears edited rows (`DIRTY=0`) and removes new, occurrence and deleted rows, which the snapshot writes back under their orOS ids. Contacts are two-way too (next bullet).
- **Two-way Contacts (v2).** The "orOS" raw contacts are written with `RAW_CONTACT_IS_READ_ONLY=0`, and `res/xml/contacts.xml` declares an `EditSchema` (name, photo, phone, email, postal, organization, nickname, website, event, note), which is what makes contacts apps treat the account as writable and offer it for new contacts (not every app does; Fossify Contacts does). Raw contacts Android marks `DIRTY` are skipped by the snapshot (kept, never removed as strays). The app sends them as `{t:"changes", what:"contacts", items:[{ref:"r<rowId>v<version>", id: SOURCE_ID|null, op, …contactRows fields, photo}]}` (thumbnail ≤ 37 000 bytes as base64). `phone.js` `applyContactChanges(blob, items, now)` (pure, tested) merges an edit over the stored contact (labels, relations, IM and website types kept; the phone photo only when orOS has none), deletes with a tombstone, and gives a new contact a new id, answered as `{t:"applied", what:"contacts", refs, ids:{ref: id}}`. The app then sets `SOURCE_ID` of new rows, clears `DIRTY` and `SYNC1` (so the snapshot rewrites the row as orOS stores it) and removes rows deleted on the phone; a row whose version changed in between stays dirty and is sent again. An open Contacts re-reads the blob through `__orosPhoneReload("contacts")` (its pull path, `setFromSync`).
- **Reminders (v3).** With `Reminders through the Android app` on (Settings › Notifications, shown only in the app; `phone.js` pref `reminders`), the page sends `{t:"reminders", seq, items:[{id, at, kind:"alarm"|"note", ns, title, body, link}]}`: the next 48 h from pure `reminderRows(src, now)` (tested). Sources are Clock alarms (`oros-alarms`, pending, daily ones each day ahead), Water `reminderDue` simulated in 5-minute steps over 24 h, and To-Do `dueSummary` at 09:00 on each day, and Health (`src.health`, `OrosHealthCore.alarmsBetween`: medicine doses not marked, snoozed ones at the snooze end, appointments at `at - rm`, vaccines at 09:00 a week before and on the day; ids `health:<key>`, deep links `health:meds|appts|vax`). Calendar is left to the phone's calendar. `id` is the shell engine's `dedupKey`; reminders already in the inbox are left out. The page re-sends when the data changes or every 5 minutes, while on screen. The app (`Reminders`, `ReminderReceiver`) stores the snapshot, arms `AlarmManager` (`setAlarmClock` for alarms, `setExactAndAllowWhileIdle` for the rest, inexact without `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM`) and re-arms after boot, update, clock or zone change. It posts to channels "Alarms" (alarm sound, insistent, 60 s) or "Reminders". A tap opens `/?phone-open=<deepLink>` → `orosNotifs.openLink`. While orOS is on screen (`{t:"seen", v}` on every visibility change and every 15 s) the app skips its reminder and the page shows its own. `localStorage` `oros-phone-rem` (`{dedupKey: at}`, this device) lists what the app was given: `notifications.js` then posts no second OS notification for those (`orosPhone.handles`), and `alarmTick` does not ring a Clock alarm late (> 60 s) that the phone already rang. State adds `reminders` (notifications: granted/ask/denied) and `exact`; `oros-permission://reminders` asks for notifications, then opens Android's exact-alarm screen.
- **Home-screen widgets (v4).** Two Android widgets: "orOS Today" (`TodayWidget`) and "orOS quick add" (`QuickWidget`); the drawing is in `Widgets`. State adds `widgets` (how many Today widgets are placed). Only while that is above 0, the page sends `{t:"today", seq, data}`: pure `widgetData(summary)` (tested) over `orosToday.build()`, i.e. the Today summary with its app on/off settings, as `{day, info, rows:[{d, tm, t, a, k}]}` (at most 30; `d` "" = a row with no day of its own). It sends at most once a minute while on screen, when the rows changed, and once more when orOS leaves the screen. The app keeps the last data (prefs "widget") and draws it again every full hour (inexact `AlarmManager.RTC`, never wakes the phone). On each draw a task whose day passed shows as late, and an event that started over an hour ago drops. Data older than two days shows "Open orOS to bring this up to date". The rows that fit follow the widget's height. Taps open `/?phone-quick=<word>`, and `phone.js` maps only these words to `__orosOpenAt`: `today` → Today, `task` → To-Do `{quickAdd}` (focuses the quick-add field), `water` → Water `{sip:"glass"}` (adds one glass today, with Undo), `note` → Notes `{newPage}` (a new empty page). Nothing is written on the phone side. Removing the last Today widget deletes the kept data.
- **Health Connect (v5).** A switch in Settings › Connected services (`secPhoneHealth`, app only; pref `health`). State adds `health`: granted / some / ask / denied / update (install or update Health Connect) / unavailable. `oros-permission://health` opens `HealthPermissionActivity`, which shows Health Connect's permission screen (or its Play page). Permissions: read steps; read and write hydration and exercise. The page sends `{t:"health", seq, since, water, workouts}` from pure `healthOut` (tested): the last 30 days of Water sips and finished Workouts, never rows that came from Health Connect (ids `hc…` / `hc-…`). It sends when they change and every 15 minutes while on screen. The app (`HealthBridge.kt`, Kotlin over `connect-client`) upserts them as its own records (clientRecordId `oros-water-<id>` / `oros-workout-<id>`, version = `m`; workouts as strength training). It deletes its own records in the window that orOS no longer has, then answers `{t:"health-in", steps:[{d,n}], water:[{ref,at,ml}], workouts:[{ref,st,en,ti,kind}]}` with OTHER apps' data only. The page applies that with pure `healthIn` (tested). Drinks become Water sips (`hc<hex>`). Workouts become Workouts rows with no exercises (`hc-<hex>`; title or a name per kind). Daily step totals become Health readings of the new built-in kind `st` (`hc-st-YYYYMMDD`; today's at now, past days at 23:59). Nothing is added over a tombstone, and an app that is open gets its share on the next answer. Switching off sends `clear` health, and the app deletes everything it wrote. The privacy page has a Health Connect section, and `HealthPrivacyActivity` (rationale / VIEW_PERMISSION_USAGE) opens it. Play needs a health-permissions declaration at upload (owner).
- **Health Connect readings (v6, Health wave 3).** Read-only permissions added: weight, resting heart rate, sleep, blood pressure, blood glucose, oxygen saturation (`android/tools/gen.js` manifest; `HealthBridge.kt` permission set). `health-in` gains `vitals:[{k wt|hr|sl|bp|gl|o2, ref, at, v:[…], c?, a?, p?}]`, OTHER apps' records only, at most 2000 per kind over the same 30 days; sleep = minutes asleep (sleep stages, else the session length); glucose in tenths of mg/dL with relation to meal → context. `healthIn` adds each as a Health reading `hc-<k>-<32 hex of ref>` once (an existing id or a tombstone is never overwritten), values range-checked (`HC_RANGE`), at most 3000 per answer. Existing installs show `some` until the user opens the switch again. Needs a new AAB and an updated Play health data-type declaration (owner).
- **Add to orOS from other apps (v2).** `AddActivity` (Android) answers calendar `INSERT` (`vnd.android.cursor.dir/event`), contacts `INSERT` / `INSERT_OR_EDIT` (after a call, from a messenger; `Insert.*` extras and `Insert.DATA` rows) and `VIEW` of .ics / .vcf (≤ 200 000 bytes), and opens orOS at `/?phone-add=<json>`: `{k:"event", date, start, end, dateEnd, title, location, note}` (times in the phone's zone; all-day UTC midnights) or `{k:"ics"|"vcf", name, text}` (a contact arrives as a one-card vCard). `phone.js` strips the parameter at once and, on `orosPhone.ready()` (shell, after apps load), hands it to `__orosOpenCalendarNew` (prefilled new event; `end` and `dateEnd` accepted) or `__orosOpenAt(…, {importIcs|importVcf})`; nothing is saved before the person confirms.
- **Calendar feeds.** The app feeds and holidays exist only as Calendar renders them, so while the Calendar switch is on `calendar.js` `phonePublish()` (after each render, debounced 1.5 s) writes the feed rows of today −14 … +180 days, labels hidden in Calendar left out, to localStorage `oros-phone-cal-feeds` `{at, items:[{k, date, start, end, title, note}]}` (this device only, never synced). `phone.js` `feedRows(store, tz)` turns them into calendar rows (id `f` + two FNV hashes of key and day, desc = feed name + note, ≤ 5000 rows) sent with `eventRows` in the same snapshot. They refresh on the phone whenever Calendar is opened.
- **Switches.** Contacts and Calendar each have "On this phone" (switch + Allow + last send). Prefs in localStorage `oros-phone` (this device only, never synced). On → sends now and whenever the slice changes (checked every 15 s while visible and on return); Off → `{t:"clear"}` removes that kind from the phone.
- **Permissions.** Android asks only from a native screen: `orosPhone.askPermission(kind)` (inside a tap) navigates to `intent://<kind>#Intent;scheme=oros-permission;package=online.useoros.twa;end`, which opens `PermissionActivity`; after "Don't ask again" it opens the app's settings.
- **Build.** `android/tools/gen.js` writes the manifest, `web_manifest.xml` and `shortcuts.xml` from `manifest.webmanifest` (not committed); `.github/workflows/android.yml` builds debug + release APK and, with the signing secrets, the signed APK and AAB. `tests/android.test.js` checks the generated manifest. Version name/code follow `APP_VERSION`.

### Opening files from the device: "Open with" → an app (BR-FILE-OPEN)
- **BR-FO-1 · Where.** Chrome / Edge with orOS installed (Windows, Linux, macOS). `manifest.webmanifest` `file_handlers` (one per app, action `/?file-open=<app>`) put orOS into the system's "Open with"; the browser asks once per type before the first launch and hands the files to `window.launchQueue`. Not in Firefox or Safari; not on Android for an installed web app (Android files come in later through the Share target or the store package). Only the person can make orOS the *default* (system settings); Settings › Opening files says how. No `launch_handler` (Dropbox OAuth, see "Send to orOS").
- **BR-FO-2 · One table.** `fileopen.js` `HANDLERS` (app → MIME → extensions) is the source; the manifest is built from it with `manifestHandlers()`, which puts each extension into its first app only (one "Open with" entry per type). `tests/fileopen.test.js` keeps the two equal. Only types an app already imports are listed; PDF, pictures, audio/video, .html, .json, .zip are not taken over on purpose. `.ics` → Calendar and `.vcf` → Contacts go through BR-FILE-IMPORT (owned by those apps): the table marks them `text: "importIcs"|"importVcf"`, the shell refuses over 5 MB, reads `file.text()` and calls `__orosOpenAt("calendar", {importIcs:{name,text}})` / `__orosOpenAt("contacts", {importVcf:{name,text}})` (no token).
- **BR-FO-3 · Choosing the app.** The person's choice for the type (localStorage `oros-file-open` `{ver:1, map:{".txt":"writer"|"ask"}}`, this device only, never synced), else the only app, else a chooser dialog in the shell ("Always use this app" saves the choice). One file per launch (more → the first, with a notice); > 50 MB refused.
- **BR-FO-4 · Handover.** A File cannot ride the JSON deep link, so the shell keeps it under a random one-shot token (10 min) and calls `__orosOpenAt(app, { openFile: { token, name, size } })`; the app takes it once with `window.parent.__orosTakeFile(token)` and runs the same import as its own Import / Open button (same size caps and sanitisers, new item or the app's own preview/confirm; nothing overwritten). Nothing is ever written back to the original file. Receivers: Writer (`ioOpenFile` → import dialog), Spreadsheet (`xlImport` / `csvImport`), Atelier (`AT.io.openFile`), Slides (`SL.io.openFile`), Layout (`LY.io.openFile`), Reader / Podcasts (`opmlFromFile`), Mind Map (`importFromFile`), Family Tree (`gedcomFromFile`), Ringtone Composer (`readImport`), Notes (`openFileTarget`).
- **BR-FO-5 · Boot.** `fileopen.js` loads before `shell.js`, strips `?file-open=` from the address bar at once and waits for `orosFileOpen.ready()` (called after `apps.json` loads). `sw.js` never caches `?file-open=` navigations.
- **BR-FO-6 · Android Share → orOS (files).** `share_target` is POST `multipart/form-data` to `/?share-target` (params title/text/url + `files`, accept = every MIME type and extension of the table, `fileopen.js` `shareTarget()`, test-checked against the manifest). `sw.js` `shareTargetPost` answers it: no file → 303 to `/?share-url=&share-title=&share-text=` (the Bookmarks path, unchanged); a file → the first one into Cache Storage `oros-share-inbox` at `/__share/<random id>` (name in `X-Name`, `X-More: 1` when there were more), 303 to `/?share-files=<id>`; > 50 MB → `/?share-files=big`. `fileopen.js` strips the param, reads the entry once, deletes the inbox, and the file goes the same way as an "Open with" file (BR-FO-3/4). Notices wait for `ready()`. The inbox survives SW activation (kept list). Needs the SW in control (always true for the installed app).
- **BR-FO-7 · Notes.** .txt / .md also open in Notes (chooser with Writer and Mind Map): a new top-level page titled after the file, text as is, ≤ 200 000 characters.
- **BR-FO-8 · Text Tools (1.18.00).** Takes .txt (after Writer, Mind Map, Notes), .csv (after Spreadsheet, so a chooser) and .tsv (only app; manifest file_handler `/?file-open=texttools`).

### CRM contracts (1.03.00)
- **BR-CRM-INV (agreed with the Invoices thread, same text in crm-plan §6 and invoices-plan §4):** CRM → Invoices `__orosOpenAt("invoices",{new:{crm?,name?,afm?,doy?,job?,addr?,country?,email?,phone?,cur?,items?:[{d,q,p}],notes?,ref?:{app,id}}})`; open `{invoice:id}` / `{client:{crm?|afm?|name?}}`. Invoices keeps `crm` on the client and every doc; read-only `invoices/core.js byCrm(data, crmId)` → rows `{id,no,date,due,total,paid,status,cur}` + per-currency totals. Invoices imports customers via `crm/core.js customersForBilling(data)`. Wired on the CRM side in phase 3.
- **CRM deep link:** `__orosOpenAt("crm", { cust | deal | fup | act: id })`; reminders `orosNotifs.emit({ns:"crm", key:"fup-<id>|<d><t>", deepLink:"crm:<fupId>"})` → opens the follow-up editor. Emitted by the app while open (closed-app reminders = phase 2).
- CRM uses: Contacts `__orosOpenContact` / `__orosOpenAt("contacts",{add:{email,name}})`, Mail compose (else mailto), Maps `__orosOpenMapsQuery`, To-Do BR-TD-ADD.

### Stock contract (planned 1.04.00, live 1.27.00)
- **BR-ST-OUT (owner Stock, live 1.27.00; sender Invoices live 1.41.01, `invoices/core.js stockOut`):** `__orosOpenAt("stock", {out: {ref?, src?: "invoices:<id>", d?, t?: "out"|"ret", lines: [{code|sku, q, p?}]}})` opens a PREFILLED sale / customer return (BR-W8-6: nothing is written until Save). `q` plain units (rounded to the unit's decimals), `p` net unit price in cents. Lines matched by SKU or barcode (`core.outRequest`); unmatched codes are listed and left out; a src already carried by live movements is warned about (count), never blocked; the saved movement keeps `src` only on the type it was opened with. Read-only `OrosStockCore.catalog(data)` → `[{id, code, name, unit, price, vat, q}]` for another app's product picker. Contract file: /mnt/project-files/stock/br-st-out.md.

### Unit Converter bridge (1.05.00)
- `__orosOpenAt("units", { cat, from, to, value })` opens a category and pair with a value (number or text); used by the search provider.

### Photo Lab edit bridge BR-PL-EDIT (Photo Lab side 1.23.00, Atelier side 1.29.02)
- Atelier → Photo Lab: `__orosOpenAt("photolab", { openFile: "/internal/Assets/<file>", back: { app: "atelier", key: "<doc id>:<element id>" } })` (back.app /^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,30}$/, key ≤ 200 chars); Photo Lab opens a new project with a "Done" button.
- Photo Lab → Atelier on Done: flattened result saved as `/internal/Assets/<sha256>.png`, then `__orosOpenAt("atelier", { editedPicture: { key, path, w, h } })`; Atelier swaps the element's picture (Undo brings the old one back). Contract: /mnt/project-files/image-editor/atelier-edit-picture-contract.md.

### Text Tools deep link (1.06.00)
- Text Tools receiver `__orosOpenAt("texttools", { text })` (≤ 2,000,000 chars): replaces the Text box with Undo; never runs anything by itself. Used by Case Converter.

### Invoices contracts (1.07.00)
- **BR-CRM-INV (agreed with CRM, same text in crm-plan §6 and invoices-plan §4):** receiver live in this release: `__orosOpenAt("invoices",{new:{crm?,name?,afm?,doy?,job?,addr?,country?,email?,phone?,cur?,items?:[{d,q,p}],notes?,ref?:{app,id}}})` opens a new invoice prefilled (an unknown client opens the New client dialog filled in); open `{invoice:id}` / `{client:{id?|crm?|afm?|name?}}`. Read-only `invoices/core.js byCrm(data, crmId)` → `{rows:[{id,kind,no,date,due,total,paid,status,cur}], totals:{CUR:{invoiced,paid,open,overdue}}}`. CRM import into Invoices clients = wave 2.
- Invoices uses: Mail compose (`__orosOpenAt("mail",{compose})` when Mail has an account, else mailto), orOS disk `orosFS.write/readBlob` for official PDFs, `orosDialog.saveFile/openFile`, Contacts and Quote data read-only for client import.

### Library ↔ Media Shelf (BR-LIB-SHELF) — live 1.11.00
- Owners: Library (`library/`) sends, Media Shelf (`shelf/`) receives. Deep link `__orosOpenAt("shelf", { addBook: { lib, title, by, year, size } })` adds the book as an e-book (or shows it if `lib` is already there).
- Each side only READS the other's slice: Library reads `oros-shelf-data` to show "Open in Media Shelf"; the Shelf reads `oros-library-data` in `libSync` (boot + visible) and writes progress as its own normal entries. Pages only move forward; a finish is logged only when Library marked the book finished on or after the run began; dropped and finished items are left alone.
- Shelf item extra field `lib` = Library book id (kept by older devices, no schema change). Pure helpers `libOf`, `libPlan`, `libItem` (shelf section 4d), tests on both sides.

### Invoices wave 2 bridges (1.13.00)
- One due rule in `invoices/core.js` (`dueOn`, `dueRows`, `reminder`) serves the Calendar "Invoices" feed chip, the Today provider `invoices/today.js` (BR-TODAY: overdue, due in the horizon, recurring drafts ready) and the shell tick (one daily notice for overdue + due within 2 days, repeated when the count grows; deep link opens the invoice).
- Senders into Invoices (`__orosOpenAt("invoices", { new })`, BR-CRM-INV payload, now also line `vat`, `disc`, `code`, `unit` and a total discount; older payloads unchanged): Quote "Make invoice" (accepted quotes), Timesheet report "Create invoice". From CRM imports customers through `crm/core.js customersForBilling()` and keeps `crm`.
- Add to Budget on a payment uses BR-B1 (Freelance income) and marks the payment `bud`.

- **BR-TODAY (CRM):** `crm/today.js`, rows = `OrosCrmCore.agenda` (late, today, horizon), kind task, `time` = the follow-up's time, target `{fup}`, Done `{done:{fup}}` → the app's `doneFup` (same as the Agenda tick: Undo + "Log it"); already done / deleted → a note, nothing written.

Never stored, micro-cached ~1 s.
- **Calendar feed "Doctor visits" / «Ιατρικά ραντεβού»** (Health wave 3): `lbl-feed-appts` pink `#f06292`, OPT-IN like Medicines; rows from `OrosHealthCore.recordOn(data, day)`: appointments at their time (end = start + duration, none across midnight) and the day a vaccine's next dose is due; click → `__orosOpenAt("health", {appt}|{vax})`.
- **Calendar feed "Customers" / «Πελάτες»:** `lbl-feed-crm` periwinkle `#8c9eff`, `calendar/index.html` loads `../crm/core.js`; rows from `OrosCrmCore.calendarOn(data, day, today)`: an open follow-up on its day at its time (late ones on today only, "Late:"), a done one on its done day ("✓"), an open deal on its expected close day (today and later); click → `__orosOpenAt("crm", {fup} | {deal})`. Never stored, micro-cached ~1 s.
- **Contacts → CRM:** the contact card shows up to 3 "Customer: <name>" / «Πελάτης: <name>» buttons (`OrosCrmCore.custsForContact`, through the shell's `OrosCrmCore`); click → `__orosOpenAt("crm", {cust})`. No CRM data → no button.

- BR-CRM-INV (CRM side live, 1.25.00): CRM → Invoices `__orosOpenAt("invoices", { new: OrosCrmCore.invoicePrefill(cust, deal?, cur) })`; Invoices → CRM read-only `OrosInvoicesCore.byCrm(OrosInvoicesCore.parse(raw), crmId, today)`.
- BR-CRM-Q (new, read-only, 1.25.00): `OrosQuoteCore.forClient(quoteData, { name, afm })` → `[{ id, num, date, due, status, cur, total }]` (total in currency units); CRM opens a row with `__orosOpenQuote(id)` and creates with `__orosOpenQuoteNew(OrosCrmCore.quotePrefill(cust, deal?, cur))`.
- BR-CRM-MAIL (receiver live in CRM since 1.29.00; sender live in Mail since 1.29.01, a "Log in CRM" button under a message): `__orosOpenAt("crm", { log: { email, name?, subject?, text?, at? } })`. email required (lower-cased, else ignored); subject ≤ 200, text ≤ 1800 chars, at = message time in ms. Prefill only.
- BR-MAIL-SIG (sender Email Signature, receiver Mail, both 1.77.00): `__orosOpenAt("mail", { signature: { html, text, name } })`. Mail opens a dialog: pick the account, preview, Use. Only Use changes the account (`sig` = text ≤ 1000, `sigHtml` = `RT.clean(html,{cid:false}).html` when rich and ≤ 60,000; m moves forward). The sender builds the HTML with `SignatureCore.build(sig, {target:"mail"})` (lines, no tables, so clean() keeps it). No accounts → toast only.

### "Send to someone" share links (BR-SHARE) — phase 1
- **What.** One item from an app becomes a link `https://<orOS>/share/#<code>`. The item lives only in the URL fragment, which browsers never send to a server; `share/index.html` opens it locally, so the other person needs no account and no orOS. Chris 2026-10-12 chose this instead of a Messages chat (Part IX).
- **Code.** Envelope `{v:1,k,d}` (k = kind, d = normalized data). Plain: `1.` + base64url(deflate-raw(JSON)), or `0.` + base64url(JSON) when `CompressionStream` is missing. Locked: `p1.` + base64url(salt16 | iv12 | AES-GCM ciphertext), key = PBKDF2-SHA256 600,000 rounds; the first plaintext byte says deflated (1) or raw (0). Password optional, off by default, at least 6 characters.
- **Limits.** Send side refuses codes over `MAX_LINK` 32,768 characters (the link buttons go off; "Save as file" still works). Decode refuses codes over MAX_LINK+8 and stops inflating past `MAX_JSON` 262,144 bytes (decompression bomb). Every field is normalized with caps in `share/kinds.js` (`norm(kind, data)`), on send and again on receive; URLs http(s) only, emails must look like emails. The page renders with `textContent` only (`view.js` has no innerHTML; `send.js` only sets the eye icon constant).
- **Kinds (phase 1).** `list` (To-Do list: title + items with note/done), `note` (Notes page title + plain text), `contact` (Contacts card without photo, labels, star, relations), `event` (Calendar event or one occurrence, UID `<id>@share.oros`), `recipe` (Meal Planner recipe), `links` (one or many Bookmarks).
- **Kind `slots` (Calendar wave 8, "Share free times").** `{ t ≤ 120, n ≤ 80 (sender name), m? (email), len 5–480 min, tz? (IANA, regex), l? ≤ 200, x? ≤ 500, s[{ d: YYYY-MM-DD, m: [minutes after midnight, sorted, unique] }] }`, ≤ 62 days, ≤ 96 per day, ≤ 1500 in all; the sender's wall times in `tz`. `target()` is null (deliver says "could not be read"): the receiving page shows the times in the receiver's own zone (`slotWhen`, Intl), hides past ones, and after a pick offers a `mailto:` back to the sender with subject/body prefilled (`slotMail`, the sender's own wall time added when the zones differ), "Add to calendar (.ics)" and "Add to my orOS" (both as kind `event` from `slotEvent`, id `slot<hash>`). Nothing is booked or stored anywhere.
- **Sender API.** `window.orosShare.open({kind, data, text?})` in the shell (apps call `parent.orosShare`). The shell lazy-loads `share/kinds.js` + `share/send.js` on first use, so they are not in index.html. Window: Share… (navigator.share), Copy link, QR code (`qr/qr-encode.js`), Email (only with a Mail account, `__orosOpenAt("mail",{compose})`), Save as file (`<name> (orOS).txt` with the link), Send as text (old behaviour, when `text` is given). Senders: To-Do `#list-share`, Notes `#btn-share-page` + page menu, Contacts card Share, Calendar `#ev-share`, Meals recipe Share, Bookmarks context menu + `#sel-share` in the selection bar.
- **Receiving.** "Add to my orOS" writes `sessionStorage["oros-share-in"] = {at,k,d}` and goes to `../?share-in=1`; the shell strips the flag and calls the module's `deliver`, which runs `__orosOpenAt(app, target)` (30 min validity). Targets from `OrosShareKinds.target(env, lang)`: list → `todo {addItems:{newList, from, items}}` (BR-TD-ADD); note → `notes {add:{title,text}}`; contact → `contacts {importVcf}` and event → `calendar {importIcs}` (BR-FILE-IMPORT, they ask before saving); recipe → `meals {addRecipe: recipe}` (new, below); links → `bookmarks {add}` for one, `{addMany}` for several (new, below). Nothing is written without the user's own Save / Import / Add, except Notes (makes a page, as its `add` always did) and Bookmarks addMany (adds, toast says how many).
- **BR-SHARE-RECIPE.** `__orosOpenAt("meals", {addRecipe: r})` — `r` goes through `OrosMealsCore.normRecipe`, loses id/m/fv, and opens in the recipe editor as a new unsaved recipe.
- **BR-BM-MANY.** `__orosOpenAt("bookmarks", {addMany:{folder, items:[{url,title}]}})` — finds the folder by name or makes it, skips URLs already in it, removes a folder it made when nothing was added, toast with the count.
- **Files.** `share/kinds.js` (pure, UMD, Node-testable), `share/send.js` (shell window), `share/index.html` + `view.js` + `share.css` (page, has inheritPalette/watchPalette for G3), help topic `help/topics/share.*.txt`, tests `tests/share.test.js`.

### Connected services contract (orosLinks, integrations wave 1)
- Apps reach another platform only through `parent.orosLinks.call(acctId, reqs)`; requests outside `OrosLinksCore.checkReq` are refused before any network call. Keys never pass through an app frame.
- Relay op `ext` (relay/ext.js): `POST /v1 {op:"ext", p, host, base, ck, cs, reqs ≤ 10}` → `{ok, data:{res:[{status, body}|{status, err:"too-big"}|{err:"timeout"|"network"}]}}`. Host checked like a mail server (public DNS, https, default port), same allowlist as the app, bodies with listed keys only, redirects not followed, writes one at a time, 2 MB per answer / 8 MB per call, 20 s per request / 28 s per call; keys never stored, logged or echoed. Owned by the Mail thread (relay/).
- Relay op `ext` for Odoo (wave 4D): `POST /v1 {op:"ext", p:"odoo", host, base, db?, key, reqs}`; host checked like WooCommerce's, `db` only for Odoo, Bearer + `X-Odoo-Database`, only the three search_read POSTs with fixed bodies (run side by side: `reads: true`).
- Relay op `ext` for Invoice Ninja (1.62.00): `POST /v1 {op:"ext", p:"ininja", host, base, key, reqs}`; host checked like WooCommerce's, `X-API-TOKEN` + `X-Requested-With`, GETs only, same allowlist as `links/core.js`.
- Relay op `ext` for Stripe (1.61.00): `POST /v1 {op:"ext", p:"stripe", key, reqs}`; restricted keys only, fixed host, GETs only, same allowlist as `links/core.js`.
- Relay op `ext` for CRMs (1.60.00): `POST /v1 {op:"ext", p:"hubspot"|"pdrive", key, reqs}`; `host`/`base`/`env` refused (fixed hosts), GETs only, same allowlist as `links/core.js`.
- Relay op `ext` for email platforms (1.59.00): `POST /v1 {op:"ext", p:"mlite"|"mchimp"|"brevo", key, reqs}`; `host`/`base`/`env` refused (fixed hosts; Mailchimp's from the key's data centre), same allowlist and body rules as `links/core.js` (incl. the Mailchimp `update_existing` rule), 64 KB per request body.
- Relay op `ext` for timologisi.online (1.58.00): `POST /v1 {op:"ext", p:"tol", env:"test"|"live", key, reqs}`; `host`/`base` refused (fixed hosts per env), header `API-KEY`, same allowlist and `okInvoice` as `links/core.js`, a write travels alone (`reqs` of 1, the app refuses more too), 64 KB request body, 65 s per request / 70 s per call (SendInvoices waits for AADE). The app gives a tol write 75 s. Any platform: a request never sent because the call's budget ran out returns `{err:"skipped"}`; `timeout`/`network` mean it may have arrived.
- Stock deep link `{view: "shop"}` opens the shop panel.

### Travel wave 31 bridges (BR-TRAVEL-MAIL, BR-SPLIT-NEW, Travel → Maps)
- **BR-TRAVEL-MAIL · Mail → Travel.** Mail's "Other apps" dialog shows "Booking to Travel" only when the message's HTML (or text) mentions `schema.org` and `Reservation` and Travel is installed. It calls `__orosOpenAt("travel", { importMail: { subject ≤ 200, html ≤ 1 MB, text ≤ 1 MB (only when there is no HTML) } })`. Mail writes nothing; the hook is isolated in `appsDialog` (`travelBooking`). Travel's receiver (`openSearchTarget` → `importFromMail`) parses with `OrosTravelBooking.parseHtml`, which uses `DOMParser("text/html")`: an inert document, scripts never run, nothing loads; only `script[type=application/ld+json]` text (JSON.parse) and microdata attributes are read. Results open in the review dialog; nothing is added until "Add". The same path serves "Import a booking" in Travel (an .eml through the lazily loaded `mail/mime.js`, an .html file, or pasted HTML).
- **Parser (`travel/booking.js`, `OrosTravelBooking`, UMD, tested in `tests/travel-booking.test.js`).** schema.org Flight / Train / Bus / Boat / Lodging / RentalCar / Taxi / FoodEstablishment / Event and generic Reservation (also `@graph`, arrays and nesting) → entries `{kind, title, from, to, day, t1, day2, t2, place, ref, num, prov, cost, ccur, note, cancelled, key}`. Times are kept as written (local, offset dropped), like the rest of Travel. One entry per flight leg; duplicates by `key` collapse. "Already in the itinerary" (`sameBooking`) = same kind and either the same booking code on the same day, or the same day, time, number, origin and title; those and cancelled ones start unticked.
- **BR-SPLIT-NEW · Travel → Split.** "Share with Split" calls `__orosOpenAt("split", { newGroup: { name, cur, people, from: "travel" } })` (`splitTarget(trip)`); Split opens its new-group dialog prefilled (see SPLIT v1). Shown only when Split is installed (`orosAssistInstalled`, as Mail's `appThere`).
- **Travel → Maps.** Maps takes at most 5 points by URL and has no multi-point API, so the itinerary map is Travel's own read-only Leaflet map (`../vendor/leaflet.js`, loaded on first use; OSM tiles) with numbered stops and straight dashed lines per day. "Save to Maps as a track" hands a GPX (`tripGpx`: waypoints + one `trkseg` per day) to the shell's BR-FILE-OPEN path (`orosFileOpen.open([File])`, the File built with the shell's `File` constructor because the Travel frame is unloaded when Maps opens); Maps imports it into My tracks. Geocoding is Photon (`photon.komoot.io`, as Maps), only on the user's "Find on the map", ≤ 60 lookups, 1 s apart, the destination first to bias the rest; a 3-letter flight code is looked up as "XXX airport". Journal tracks open with `__orosOpenAt("maps", { track: id })`.

## Part VII — UI standards

- **Scrollbars:** 10px, transparent track, pill thumb (999px radius, 2px border `var(--bg)`), hover `var(--accent)`; Firefox `scrollbar-width:thin`. `overscroll-behavior:contain` on main panes.
- **Hidden guard:** `[hidden]{display:none!important}` is the LAST rule of every app stylesheet.
- **Icons:** inline SVG with viewBox + explicit size (Fork Awesome abandoned).
- **Toasts:** a stack (newest first, max 5 visible, promote on removal). Default bottom-right; the notifications `position` setting moves it live, and bottom positions grow upward. Text first, action second. Undo toasts ≥ 8 s. **[log]**
- **Centered popups (R32) [log]:**
  1. A native `<dialog>` MUST declare `margin: auto`. Every app stylesheet has `* { margin: 0 }`, which kills the UA default and docks the dialog top-left. Recommended: `margin: auto; max-height: calc(100vh - 32px);`.
  2. An overlay panel (not a `<dialog>`) uses `position: absolute; top: 50%; left: 50%; transform: translate(-50%, -50%)` inside a fixed full-inset overlay (`position: fixed; inset: 0`). No inline `style.top` / `style.left` from JS anchor math.
  3. A flex overlay centers with `margin: auto` ON THE PANEL, never with `align-items: center` on the container: a panel taller than the viewport would lose its top to clipping, unreachable by scroll. Reference: Contacts view card (`#ct-view` + `.ct-view-card`).
  4. Long content scrolls inside the popup (`overflow-y: auto` + `max-height`).
  5. Exception: context menus (`#ctx-menu`) stay anchored at the pointer.
- **Z-index ladder [log]:** boot splash 9999 · `#oros-toast-stack` 10000 · inbox panel 10001. Toasts never fall behind the splash.
- **Observers [log]:** a `MutationObserver` watches the element that actually parents the node. A generic `document.body` observer silently never fires for children of another container.
- **Selectors [log]:** never key CSS or JS on localized text (`[title*="remove"]` broke under Greek). Check specificity before adding an override: an id selector beats a class block.
- **Key handling in a frame [log]:** keys reach only the focused browsing context. Numpad keys are matched by `e.code` (with NumLock off, `e.key` is "End", "PageUp"…). Blur a clicked button so Enter/Space do not re-trigger it.
- **NOTIFICATIONS ≠ TOASTS:** cross-session/event reminders → `emit()` (inbox + badge + history); in-context feedback → transient/local toast.
- **Mobile:**
  - single-thumb reach; touch targets ≥44px; safe-area `env()` insets; breakpoints 480/420/360;
  - long-press 450ms as the touch twin of right-click menus (every right-click/Alt-click feature needs a touch path).
  - **Toolbars wider than a phone scroll horizontally** (single strip, hidden scrollbar), never clip.
- **Desktop:** ≥1024px split views allowed.
- **Editor toolbars:** formatting buttons `preventDefault()` on `mousedown` so the editor keeps focus and selection (touch collapsed it).
- **DOM stability:** don't rebuild a container on click when a dblclick may follow (the 2nd click lands on a new node → no dblclick). Update classes in place.
- **Interactive containers:** no `<input>` inside a `<button>`. Use `div[role=tab][tabindex=0]` with Enter/Space/F2 handlers.
- **Find/highlight:** never move the document selection while the user types in a search field (Chrome moves focus → keystrokes overwrite the match). After unwrapping highlight marks, `normalize()` the parents.
- **Autosave:** debounce, no Save buttons for settings; flush on `visibilitychange→hidden` and `pagehide`.
- **Deleting:** danger styling; Undo toast (R17 resurrection) preferred over confirmations.
- **Language:** EN/EL only; EL dates ηη/μμ/εεεε, no comma after the day.
- **Version badge:** shell Info modal only.
